sections.title: 22-32 ALLAH BLESSED THE MAN WHO BELIEVED WITH PARADISE AND DESTROYED THE DISBELIEVERS

translation.text: Why should I not serve the One Who created me and to Whom all of you shall be sent back?

commentary.text: This sentence has two parts.
The first part contains the wisdom of reasoning: To not worship the Creator and instead worship the creation is highly irrational. So think and reflect – don’t just follow blindly.

The second part has the acumen of preaching. He warns his people to the effect: All of you ultimately have to die and return to that God that you deny. Therefore, what goodness can you expect from Allah SWT when you spent your life denying Him (being ungrateful).

translation.text: What! Shall I take any deities apart from Him whose intercession will not avail me the least were the Merciful One to bring any adversity upon me, nor will they be able to rescue me?

commentary.text: The false gods or deities are neither such favorites of Allah SWT that if I commit serious sins or crimes Allah SWT will forgive me on their recommendation/intercession nor are they so powerful that they will be able to rescue me if Allah SWT wants to punish me.
He asks a rhetorical question forcing the mushriks to think. He does not attack them directly.
This is a golden rule or principle of preaching/giving dawah i.e. encourage people to reflect and think for themselves without making them feel defensive or attacked.

translation.text: Surely in that case I should indeed be in evident error.

commentary.text: If I make these false deities my gods in spite of knowing all this (the truth) – then that is a huge mistake.
The man makes himself the subject/object by saying "I" will be in error.
Again, this is a good way to give dawah by being inclusive and not alienating or pointing fingers at anyone.

translation.text: I believe in your Lord; so listen to me.

commentary.text: Here again we find a subtlety regarding the wisdom of preaching or giving dawah. "Your Lord," implies the Lord in whom I have believed is not merely my Lord but your Lord, too. I have committed no error by believing in Him, but you, in fact, are certainly committing an error by not believing in Him.

translation.text: (Eventually they killed him and he was told): “Enter Paradise.” The man exclaimed: “Would that my people knew

commentary.text: Immediately following his martyrdom, the man was given the good news of Paradise. As soon as he entered the next world through the gate of death there were angels to receive him and they give him the good news that Paradise was awaiting him.

translation.text: for what reason Allah has forgiven me and placed me among the honoured ones.”

commentary.text: The noble person did not wish Hell for his murderers but wished that they should believe and become worthy of Paradise. This same opinion has been mentioned in the Hadith: "He wished his people well when living as well as when dead".

Allah SWT has narrated this event in order to warn the disbelievers of Makkah that Muhammad (PBUH) and his believing companions are also your well-wishers just as the believer was for his people. They do not harbor any ill-will or feelings of vengeance against you in spite of your persecutions against them. They are not your enemies but enemies of your deviation and error. The only object of their struggle against you is that you should adopt the right way.

This Ayat also proves the existence of barzakh. This shows that the period of time between death and Resurrection is not a period of nonexistence altogether. But in this period the spirit lives without the body, speaks and hears speech, has feelings and desires, feels happy and unhappy, and also continues to be concerned about the people of the world. Had it not been so, the believer would not have been given the good news of Paradise after death, and he could not have wished that his people became aware of his good end. (Maududi)

translation.text: After him, We did not send down any hosts from the heaven; We stood in no need to send down any host.
There was but a single Blast and suddenly they became silent and still.

commentary.text: In their arrogance and hunger for power they thought they would annihilate the three Prophets and their followers but contrary to their plot they themselves were annihilated and that too by only one stroke of the divine punishment.

sections.title: 33-36 ALLAH HAS CREATED ALL THINGS IN PAIRS

arabic_lines: وَاٰيَةٌ لَّهُمُ الۡاَرۡضُ الۡمَيۡتَةُ ۖۚ اَحۡيَيۡنٰهَا وَاَخۡرَجۡنَا مِنۡهَا حَبًّا فَمِنۡهُ يَاۡكُلُوۡنَ

translation.text: Let the dead earth be a Sign for them. We gave it life and produced from it grain whereof they eat.

commentary.text: Proof of the Creator of the Universe and of Life after Death
Until now the disbelievers of Makkah were being warned and reprimanded for their denial of the truth and their attitude of resentment/rivalry towards the Prophet (PBUH).

Now the discourse turns to the basic/fundamental principle that was the cause of conflict between the disbelievers of Makkah and the Prophet (PBUH) that is the doctrine of Tauhid, Prophet hood and the Hereafter. In this regard consecutive arguments have been provided so as to compel people to contemplate and observe the realities of this universe.
“A sign وَاٰيَةٌ ”: A sign that Tauhid is the truth and shirk the falsehood.

translation.text: We made in it gardens of date-palms and vines, and We caused springs to gush forth
that they might eat of its fruits. It was not their hands that made them. Will they not, then, give thanks?

commentary.text: Here vegetable and plant life on earth have been presented as an argument for Tauhid. Man is eating what has been produced from the earth and regarding this phenomenon as ordinary. But if he considers it seriously, he will see that the growth of crops and lush greenery from the dry earth is not a simply happening by itself, rather there is a great system, wisdom, power and providence working behind it.

The question is: How did it become possible for plant life to emerge from the lifeless earth? Who constructs the perfect harmony and balance between the soil, irrigation, atmosphere and temperature so as to bring forth vegetation? Anyone who ponders over this wonderful arrangement, will himself testify that all this could not have come about by itself. There is certainly a wise plan underlying it and this is not just a mere accident.

After giving these arguments for Tauhid, Allah SWT says: Do they not then give thanks? That is: Are these people so thankless and ungrateful that they do not render thanks to that God Who has provided all this for their survival but instead they thank others for the blessings and favors done by Him? Are they so wretched that instead of bowing before Him they bow before the false gods, who have not created even a blade of grass for them?

arabic_lines: سُبۡحٰنَ الَّذِىۡ خَلَقَ الۡاَزۡوَاجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنۡۢبِتُ الۡاَرۡضُ وَمِنۡ اَنۡفُسِهِمۡ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعۡلَمُوۡنَ

translation.text: Glory be to the One Who created all things in pairs, whether it be of what the earth produces, and of themselves, and of what they do not know.

commentary.text: "Glory be to Him سُبۡحٰنَ الَّذِىۡ" The Quran generally uses these words when refuting the mushrik's beliefs because every belief of shirk is an assertion of some defect, weakness or fault towards Allah SWT. When a person says that Allah SWT has an associate, he in fact, thinks that either Allah SWT is incapable of ruling His Kingdom alone or He is under compulsion to make another an associate in His work. Or some other beings are so powerful that they are interfering in God’s administration and God is putting up with their interference.

Another argument for Tauhid. The creation of pairs whether it be in the form of what is in the universe I.e. sun/moon, earth/sky or in within humans themselves i.e. male/female there is a wisdom regarding the perfect harmony and complementary nature between the members of each pair and thus this cannot be regarded as an unplanned coincidence.
Allah SWT does not need a pair.

sections.title: 37-40 DAY, NIGHT, SUN AND MOON; ALL ARE BEING REGULATED BY ALLAH

translation.text: And the night is another Sign for them. We strip the day from it and they become plunged in darkness.

commentary.text: Among the Signs of the Might and Power of Allah are the Night and Day, and the Sun and Moon

The seamless and majestic alternation of night and day is one of those miracles which man does not regard as worthy of much attention maybe because it is a daily occurrence and experience, whereas if he considers the wisdom and logic behind the passing of the day and the falling of the night, he will himself realize that this is an obvious sign of the existence of an All-Powerful and All-Wise Allah SWT.

The absolute regularity in the rotation of night and day would not be possible unless the sun and the earth were bound in one system. Thus, the relationship that exists between the alternation of the day and night and the other creations on the earth clearly point to the fact that this system has been established deliberately by a Being with perfect wisdom.

The existence on the earth, of man, animals vegetation, and even of water, air and different minerals, is in fact, the result of placing the earth at a particular distance from the sun, with the arrangement that the different parts of the earth should go on successively coming before the sun and hiding from it at definite intervals.

If the distance of the earth from the sun had been a little longer or a little shorter or there had been a perpetual nighttime on one side of it and a perpetual daytime on the other, or the alternation of the day and night had been much faster or much slower, no life could be possible on this planet.
Thus, to ascribe this intricate, interlinked system to many gods/deities or to think that all this has happened automatically under some deaf and blind law of nature is gravely erroneous.
If hearts are not blinded, one can clearly perceive, in this system, the working of Allah SWT.

translation.text: The sun is running its course to its appointed place. That is the ordaining of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.

commentary.text: “To it's appointed place..” may either mean the place where the sun will ultimately come to a halt, or the time when it will come to a halt. The true meaning of this Ayat can be determined only when man has attained the full and exact knowledge of the realities of the universe. But man’s knowledge is such that it has been changing in every age and what he seems to know today might change tomorrow.

The people of ancient times, on the basis of their observations of the sun, believed that the sun was moving round the earth. However, after further research and observation the view became that the sun was stationary and all the planets of the solar system were revolving round it. But this theory also did not last long.

The later observations revealed that not only the sun but all the stars are also moving in a particular direction, at speeds of 10 to 100 miles per second. About the sun the modern astronomers hold the view that it is moving at a speed of 20 kilometers (about 12 miles) per second along with its whole family of the planets. Nothing is random. Everything is happening with Allah SWT’s decree.

translation.text: We have appointed stages for the moon till it returns in the shape of a dry old branch of palm-tree.

commentary.text: The phases of the moon go on changing throughout the month. It begins as a crescent, then goes on waxing every day till it becomes the full moon on the 14th of the month. Then it starts waning every day till at last it returns to its original shape of the crescent – resembling a dry old branch of palm tree. This has been happening for millions of years with perfect regularity.

translation.text: Neither does it lie in the sun's power to overtake the moon nor can the night outstrip the day.  All glide along, each in its own orbit.

commentary.text: It is not possible that the sun should suddenly appear on the horizon when the moon is shining at night.
Nor does the night approach before the appointed period of the day comes to an end.

The vastness of the solar system, in which our earth is included, is such that its parent body, the sun, is 300,000 times bigger than the earth and its farthest planet Neptune is at least 2,793 million miles distant from the sun. Notwithstanding this vastness, the solar system occupies a very insignificant part of a huge galaxy. The galaxy that includes our solar system has about 3,000 million suns in it and its nearest sun is so distant from our earth that its light takes about four years to reach us.

These Ayats (signs) are not intended to describe the realities of astronomy rather are meant to make man understand that if he/she looks around he/she will find countless proofs of the existence of God. Is it possible that there should be no administrator, planning or wisdom behind this flawless order?
Lesson: Consistently doing the same thing over and over again will eventually result in excellence. Look around within the universe for examples.

sections.title: 41-50 DISBELIEVER'S ATTITUDE TOWARDS SPENDING IN THE WAY OF ALLAH

translation.text: And when it is said to them: “Spend (in the Way of Allah) out of the sustenance that Allah has provided you,” the unbelievers say to the believers: “Shall we feed him whom, Allah would have fed, had He so wished?” Say: “You are in evident error.”

commentary.text: The muhsriks did not want to part with their money so they used the excuse that, if Allah SWT is All Mighty then surely, he could have fed the poor or needy Himself. Why should we feed those whom Allah SWT could have fed or does not want to feed?

translation.text: They say: “When will this threat (of Resurrection) come to pass? Tell us if indeed you are truthful.”

commentary.text: The Disbelievers thought that the Day of Resurrection would never come to pass

After Tauhid the other matter about which a dispute was raging between the Prophet (PBUH) and the disbelievers was the question of the Hereafter. Questions about Resurrection were put as a challenge only for the sake of argument as they (disbelievers) felt Resurrection was impossibility. That is why in reply it has not been said that Resurrection will take place on such and such a day but that it shall come and shall be accompanied by such and such horrors.

translation.text: The Truth is that they are waiting for nothing but a mighty Blast to seize them the while they are disputing (in their worldly affairs)
and they will not even be able to make a testament, nor to return to their households.

commentary.text: Resurrection will not take place piecemeal so that the people may leisurely watch its coming but it will come all of a sudden when people are busy in their daily lives/business. There will be a terrible blast and everyone will fall dead at that spot.
Hadith: Prophet (PBUH) said:

People will be walking on the roads as usual, buying and selling in the markets, disputing matters in their assemblies, when suddenly the Trumpet shall be sounded. Thereupon the one who was buying cloth will collapse not having time to put down the cloth and the one who was going to eat will not have time to lift the morsel to his mouth and thus Resurrection will take place.

sections.title: 51-54 A SCENE FROM THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT

translation.text: Then the Trumpet shall be blown and lo! they will come out of their graves and be on the move towards their Lord

commentary.text: For the explanation of the blowing of the Trumpet, see (E.N. 78 of Surah TaHa). As for the length of the interval between the first blowing of the Trumpet and its second blowing, we have no information.
Hadith: Prophet (PBUH) said:
Israfil has put the Trumpet to his mouth and is looking up to the divine Throne awaiting orders for blowing it. The Trumpet will be blown thrice.
On the first blowing, called 'nafakhat al-faza' everything in the earth and heavens will be struck with terror.

On the second blowing, called 'nafakhat as-Saaq', everyone will fall down dead. Then, when none shall remain except Allah SWT, the earth will be changed altogether and spread flat and smooth without a crease or wrinkle on it.
On the third blowing of the Trumpet called 'nafakhat al qiyam li-Rabbil-Alamin', upon Allah SWT's command everyone will rise at the spot where he/she had fallen dead, on the changed earth.
Also, see (Surah Ibrahim, Ayat 48); (Surah TaHa, Ayats 105-108)

translation.text: (nervously) exclaiming. “Alas for us! Who roused us out of our sleeping-place?” “This is what the Merciful One had promised, and what (His) Messengers had said was true.”

commentary.text: At that time people will not realize that they have been dead and raised back to life rather they will think that they have been arise from sleep by some terrible catastrophe and are running away from it.
(For further details, see Surahs (TaHa, Ayat 103); (Al-Hajj, Ayats 1-2).
Then they will realize that this is the very thing the Messengers of God used to inform them about and they used to deny it.

translation.text: Then there will simply be one single Blast, and all will have gathered before Us.
Today no one shall suffer the least injustice, and you shall not be recompensed except according to your deeds.

commentary.text: This is a beautiful Ayat for those who do right. Otherwise, a very frightening one.

sections.title: 55-58 ALLAH'S GREETING TO THE RESIDENTS OF PARADISE

translation.text: Indeed, the people of Paradise will be busy enjoying themselves:

commentary.text: The Life of the People of Paradise

The righteous believers will not be held in the Plain of Resurrection rather from the very beginning they will be sent to Paradise without accountability or after a mild reckoning because their record will be clean.

Allah SWT will tell the culprits, who will be required to render their accounts, in the Plain of Resurrection: ‘Look! the righteous people whom you used to mock and regard as foolish in the world are today enjoying the pleasures of Paradise because of their wisdom, while you are being condemned to accountability for your misdeeds.’

translation.text: they and their spouses shall be reclining on their couches in shady groves;
therein there will be all kinds of fruits to eat, and they shall have all that they desire
“Peace”( سَلٰمٌ )shall be the word conveyed to them from their Merciful Lord.

commentary.text: Allah SWT will greet the inhabitants of Heaven with "Salam." These are the blessings of Heaven.

sections.title: 59-67 ALLAH'S ADDRESS TO THE CRIMINAL SINNERS AND ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT HANDS AND FEET SHALL TESTIFY

translation.text: “Criminals, separate yourselves from others today!

commentary.text: Day of Judgment will also be the day of separation. This Ayat can have two meanings:
(1) Separate yourself from the righteous believer. Even if you belonged to the same community, clan and brotherhood in this world here you have no connection and relationship left with them.
(2) Separate yourself from one another. All your relations and connections have been severed. Now each of you will be held answerable in your personal capacity for your actions and deeds.

translation.text: Children of Adam, did I not command you not to worship Satan? he is to you an open enemy
and serve Me alone: this is the Straight Way?

commentary.text: Do not worship Satan means: Do not obey him. Satan has been declared as your open enemy by Allah SWT so take heed.

translation.text: Still, he misguided a whole throng of you. Did you have no sense?

commentary.text: Man, has been blessed with intellect and reason yet despite Allah SWT 's warning that "satan is your clear/open enemy," still satan has succeeded in his deception by leading many many astray.

translation.text: Now this is the Hell of which you were warned.
Burn in it on account of your disbelieving.

commentary.text: Now you cannot be excused from the responsibility of your folly. So suffer the consequences.

translation.text: Today We shall put a seal on their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us and their feet shall bear witness to what they had been doing.

commentary.text: The Mouths of the Disbelievers will be sealed on the Day of Resurrection

This command will be given for those stubborn culprits who refuse to confess their crimes, deny witnesses, and also do not acknowledge the genuineness of their conduct-book. Then by Allah SWT's command their own limbs will testify to their misdeeds.

In this connection only hands and the feet have been mentioned here. However, in other places it has been said that their eyes, and their ears, their tongues, and the skins of their body will testify regarding how they had been employed in the world i.e. what lies, mischief, falsehoods they were made to do or utter. See below:
They should not forget the Day when their own tongues and their own hands and feet will bear testimony to their misdeeds. (Surah An-Noor, Ayat 24)
Then, when all will have reached there, their ears and their eyes and their very skins will bear witness against them concerning what they had been doing in the world. (Surah HaMim-Sajdah, Ayat 20).

translation.text: If We so willed, We would have put out their eyes, then they would rush to see the Way, but how would they be able to see?
If We so willed, We would have transformed them where they were so that they would not go forward or backward.

commentary.text: After depicting the scene of Resurrection, people are being warned against being too proud on this earth and to understand their fragility. With one command Allah SWT can take away our sight and or abilities.

As long as the powers and capabilities granted by Allah SWT continue to function we remain lost in arrogance and the delusions of this world but as soon as we are rendered helpless (by Allah SWT) we realize just how feeble/dependent we indeed are.

sections.title: 68-76 AL-QURAN IS TO WARN THOSE WHO ARE ALIVE AND TO ESTABLISH CHARGE AGAINST THE DISBELIEVERS

translation.text: We did not teach him (to wit, the Messenger) poetry and it does not behove him. This is none but an Admonition, and a Clear Book

commentary.text: Allah does not teach His Messenger Poetry

This is a response to the disbelievers who insulted the Prophet (PBUH) and his message by branding him a poet when he preached the doctrine of Tauhid, the Hereafter, life-after-death, Hell and Heaven.
(For further explanation, see (Surah Ash-Shuara, Ayats 224-227)

Allah SWT says the Quran is not poetry and it does not befit the Prophet (PBUH) to say poetry.  Poetry contains exaggeration/lies. The kalamat of Allah SWT are based on truth and the message is very clear.

arabic_lines: لِّيُنۡذِرَ مَنۡ كَانَ حَيًّا وَّيَحِقَّ الۡقَوۡلُ عَلَى الۡكٰفِرِيۡنَ

translation.text: that he may warn him who is alive and establish an argument against those that deny the Truth.

commentary.text: This Quran is an unambiguous and direct Book that warns those who are alive; meaning their fitra (soul and heart) is alive. Some people are alive in the sense that they are capable of seeing and walking but their ruh are dead thus they cannot distinguish between truth and falsehood.
The Quran is not meant to be read only at the time of death but is meant for the living.

sections.title: 77-83 ALLAH, WHO HAS CREATED THE MAN, SHALL GIVE HIM LIFE AGAIN, FOR ACCOUNTABILITY ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT

translation.text: Does man not see that We created him of a sperm drop, and lo! he is flagrantly contentious?
And they argue with Us—forgetting they were created—saying, “Who will give life to decayed bones?”
Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “They will be revived by the One Who produced them the first time, for He has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of every created being.

commentary.text: Context: One of the chiefs of Makkah brought a rotten bone of a dead person from the graveyard. He broke and crushed it into pieces before the Prophet (PBUH) and scattering its particles in the air and said: ‘O Muhammad, you say that the dead will be raised back to life. Tell us who will give life to these decayed and rotten bones’? The answer was given immediately in the form of these Ayats above.

Allah SWT caused the sperm-drop which contained nothing but the basic germ of life to develop powers of intellect, reasoning, disputation and speech, which are not possessed by any animal, so much so that now Man dares stand up as an adversary before his very Creator!

translation.text: Whenever He wills a thing, He just commands it “Be” and it is

commentary.text: Allah SWT only needs to command a thing once; it does not need to be repeated nor confirmed. When Allah SWT intends for something, He only has to say “Be" and it happens.

translation.text: Glory be to Him Who has full control over everything, and to Him you shall all be recalled.

commentary.text: All praise and exaltation is only for Allah SWT who is supreme over ALL. And to Allah SWT we will all return.
Emphasis of this Surah is the Hereafter – so Prepare!

These Ayats (signs) are not intended to describe the realities of astronomy rather are meant to make man understand that if he/she looks around, he/she will find countless proofs of the existence of God. Is it possible that there should be no administrator, planning or wisdom behind this flawless order?
THE QURAN IS OUR GATEWAY TO HEAVEN
(36:70) that he may warn him who is alive and establish an argument against those that deny the Truth.
This Quran is a clear, precise, simple and direct Book that warns those who are alive; meaning their fitra (soul and heart) is alive.
THE HEREAFTER IS A CERTAINTY
Prepare!

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The name is derived from the word saaffat with which the Surah begins.

items.text: وَالصّٰٓفّٰتِ صَفًّا (As-Saffat)
(37:1) By those who range themselves in rows;

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makki Surah and it was revealed sometime during the middle Makkan period.  It has 182 Ayats in 5 Rukus.

front_matter.label: Subject Matter and Theme
front_matter.text:
This Makkan surah, like the previous surah Ya Sin, is composed of short Ayats and is characterized by fast beats, successive scenes and a myriad of images. Indeed, the effect it produces at times is very intense.

Like all Makkan revelations, its aim is to establish the Islamic faith firmly in people’s hearts, purging it of any traces of idolatry and shirk. In this respect it addresses a particular form of shirk that prevailed in Arabian society that God has a lineage with the jinns, and the angels are His daughters.

The surah discusses the various Prophets of Allah SWT.  All of them sermonized the same message of Tawhid and the Hereafter.

The last Ayat’s of this surah are not only a warning for the disbelievers that their plots against the message of Islam will not work but also gives good news for the believers who were passing through highly unfavorable and discouraging conditions on account of their supporting and following the Holy Prophet.

They were given the good news that in the end they will attain dominance, and the standard bearers of falsehood who appeared to be dominant at the time will be overwhelmed and vanquished at their hands. A few years later the turn the events proved that it was not an empty consolation but an inevitable reality of which they had been foretold in order to strengthen their hearts.

sections.title: 1-11 ALLAH TESTIFIES THAT YOUR GOD IS ONE GOD AND THAT SHAITANS DO NOT HAVE AND EXCESS TO THE EXALTED ASSEMBLY OF ANGELS

translation.text: By those who range themselves in rows;

commentary.text: Also see (37:165)

Allah SWT takes an oath, by the angels, who are administering the affairs of the universe. They are the humble, obedient servants of Allah SWT, who are in complete submission and ever ready to implement His commands. They arrange themselves in orderly rows -- ready to serve. They are collectively and personally organized ready to implement any order from their Raab.
This theme of rows has been further repeated: (37:165) Verily we range ourselves in rows (as humble servants).

translation.text: Who rebuke reproachfully

commentary.text: The oath continues; by those angels who scold and curse the disobedient people. This scolding and cursing are not merely verbal but also via natural disasters and calamities.

translation.text: And recite God’s word,

commentary.text: The oath continues; by those angels who recite the Quran, do zikr and bring down Allah SWT's teachings (wahi) to the Prophets, for example, Angel Gabriel. These angels are never heedless to Allah SWT's remembrance.

translation.text: surely your God is One

commentary.text: The One True God is Allah. All angels witness to the Oneness of Allah
This is the conclusion to the oath. 'There is only one God – Allah SWT.'
Context: Here the false belief of Arabs that angels are the daughters of Allah SWT is being refuted. Angels are only carrying out the orders/commands of Allah SWT.

arabic_lines: رَبُّ السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالۡاَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ الۡمَشَارِقِ ؕ

translation.text: the Lord of the Heavens and the earth and of whatever lies between the two, the Lord of the Easts.

commentary.text: Allah SWT alone is the Master and Ruler of the Universe. The basic reason for worship is that man should naturally bow down before and acknowledge the superiority of Allah SWT who fulfills man’s needs and requirements, who can make or mar his destiny and has power over his life and survival itself.
"Lord of the Easts"

The sun does not always rise at the same point or same time. That is why the plural “mashariq” (Easts) has been used to indicate the different points at which the sun rises according to the season of the year. Every place thus is the East at some point.

translation.text: We have adorned the lower Heaven with the adornment of the stars

commentary.text: One purpose of stars in the sky is beautification. “Lower Heaven”: The nearest Heaven that can be seen with the naked eye, without the help of a telescope.

translation.text: and have protected it from every rebellious satan.

commentary.text: Another purpose of stars is to prevent Jinns from going up to the skies and listening to the angels.

At the outset, the surah touches on the part of the superstition that relates to angels. Now it touches on the part that relates to the jinn. In pre-Islamic days, some Arabs alleged that the jinn were related to God. Indeed, some of them worshipped the jinn for this reason, and because they attributed to them knowledge of the unseen.

translation.text: These satans cannot listen to what transpires in the High Council for they are pelted away from every side

commentary.text: The satans or Jinns cannot reach the 'higher group' or 'high council' -- which refers to the assembly of angels in Heaven -- to listen to their conversations when they speak of what has been revealed by Allah SWT regarding His Laws and decrees.  Jinns are pelted with burning hot flames (shooting stars).

translation.text: and are repelled. Theirs is an unceasing chastisement.
And if any is able to snatch a fragment, he is pursued by a piercing flame.

commentary.text: In the time of the Prophet (PBUH), soothsaying was very prevalent in Arabia. The soothsayers used to make predictions, give news of the unseen, tell the whereabouts of the lost properties and articles and people used to visit them to know the events of their past and future lives. These soothsayers claimed that they had jinns and satans under their control who brought them all sorts of news.

In this environment when the Prophet (PBUH) was appointed to Prophethood and he began to recite the Ayat’s of the Quran, which described the past history and contained news of the future, and also stated that an angel brought him these Ayat’s, his opponents immediately branded him a soothsayer and started telling others that, like the other soothsayers, he too was associated with a satan, who brought him news from the Heavens, which he presented as revelations from Allah SWT.

To refute this accusation, Allah SWT says: The satans or Jinns have no access to Heaven. They have no power to hear the conversations of the angels and bring news for others. If by chance a little of it enters the ear of a satan, and he tries to bring it down, he is followed by a flashing flame.
(For further explanation, see (Surah Al-Hijr, Ayats 17-18 )

Except for the one/some among the shayatin/satans who manages to get something which is a word he has heard from the Heaven. Then he throws it down to the one who is beneath him, who in turn throws it down to the one who is beneath him. Perhaps the flaming fire will strike him before he is able to throw it down, or perhaps he will throw it -- by the decree of Allah SWT-- before the flaming fire strikes him and burns him. So, the other devil takes it to the soothsayer.

translation.text: So ask them (that is, human beings): “Were they harder to create than the objects We created?”8 We created them from sticky clay

commentary.text: The Certainty of Life after Death
This is an answer to the doubts of the disbelievers of Makkah regarding the Hereafter. They thought that the Hereafter is an impossibility.

Allah SWT says: Why don’t you use your common sense? Do you think that God for Whom it was not at all difficult to create the earth, mountains, skies and this great universe and Who has created you in the first instance, will not have the power to create you once again?

That is, man is not a difficult thing to make. He has been created from clay and can again be created from the same clay. “Created them from sticky clay” means that the first man was created directly from the clay and then his race was perpetuated by means of the sperm drop. Man is reminded of his humble origin and that he is weak -- So do not Reject!

sections.title: 12-21 LIFE IN THE HEREAFTER AND THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT ARE REAL

translation.text: Is it ever possible that after we die and are reduced to dust and (a skeleton of) bones, we will be raised to life?
And so also shall our forefathers of yore be raised to life?”
Tell them: “Yes; and you are utterly helpless (against Allah).”

commentary.text: Allah SWT says, "YES!" Resurrection will occur! With one command by Him you will die and then whenever He wills; His one command will raise you back to life.

translation.text: They will then say: “Woe for us. This is the Day of Judgment.”

commentary.text: The Day of Recompense also The Day of Regret also The Day of Separation

Allah SWT tells us what the disbeliever will say on the Day of Resurrection; when they see the horrors of the Day of Resurrection with their own eyes. They will be filled with regret at the time when regret will not avail them any good/benefit. This is also a Day of separation when people will be gathered with the group they sinned with.

translation.text: “Yes, this is the Day of Final Decision that you used to deny as a lie.”

commentary.text: In this world you lived in a way as if no Day of Judgment would ever come. Now you have come to your doom. This is the same Day that you used to deny.

sections.title: 22-39 A SCENE FROM THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT AND A TREATMENT FOR THE WRONGDOERS AND A DIALOGUE BETWEEN THE FOLLOWERS AND THE LEADERS WHO MISLEAD THEM

translation.text: (Then will the command be given to the angels): “Muster all the wrong-doers and their spouses and the deities whom they used to serve

commentary.text: 'The wrongdoers,' does not only imply those who committed sins in the world but the term 'Zulum' or 'injustice,' also means those who committed shirk.

People will be in groups with those who were like them i.e. those who committed zina will be gathered with others who committed zina, those who dealt in riba (interest) will be gathered with others who dealt in riba (interest), those who drank wine will be gathered with others who drank wine, etc.

translation.text: apart from Allah, and direct them to the path of Hell,

commentary.text: These people will then be led to the path towards Hell.

translation.text: and detain them there; they will be called to account.

commentary.text: These people will then be questioned by Allah SWT regarding their deeds during their time on earth.

translation.text: How is it that you are not helping one another?
Indeed, today they are surrendering themselves completely.”

commentary.text: Ayat (37:25) will be addressed to the culprits, and the second (37:26) to the common spectators, who will be watching the scene of the culprit’s departure for Hell. A description of how the haughty and stubborn culprits of the world will now be moving meekly/feebly towards Hell without showing any resistance.
Somewhere a King will be seen being pushed about and no one from among his courtiers will come forward to rescue 'his majesty.'
Somewhere a saint or some holy person will be seen being thrown into Hell and no one of his disciples will bother to save him from disgrace.

By depicting this scene Allah SWT wants to impress how the relationships of man with man which are based on rebellion against Allah SWT in the world, will break in the Hereafter and how the pride of those who are involved in arrogance and conceit here on earth will come crumbling down.

translation.text: They will then turn towards each other (and start wrangling).
(The followers will say to their leaders): “You used to come to us from the right hand.”

commentary.text: The arguing of the Idolators on the Day of Resurrection

Allah SWT tell us that the followers will say to their leaders that this is all your fault and you are the reason we are now rotting in Hell. You approached us from the right hand or 'yameen'.  The Arabic word 'yameen' in this Ayat means:
(1) You compelled us into following error and deviation.
(2) You deceived us by posing as our well-wishers.
(3) You swore oaths to satisfy us that what you were presenting was the very truth.

translation.text: They will say: “Nay, you yourselves were not the ones who would believe.

commentary.text: The leaders will say: don’t blame us because if you truly believed (had Iman) you would not have been swayed so easily.

translation.text: On that Day, they will all share the chastisement.

commentary.text: Both the leaders and their followers shall all suffer the same torment. Neither will the follower's excuse be heeded that they did not go astray but led astray nor the guides/leaders excuse be accepted that the people themselves were not desirous of following the right path.

translation.text: Thus do We treat the culprits.
Whenever it was said to them: “There is no true deity apart from Allah,” they waxed proud
And said, ‘Are we to forsake our gods for a mad poet?’
You will only be recompensed according to your deeds.”

commentary.text: This punishment is a recompense for only what you did. This is good news for the righteous and terrible information for the disbelievers.

sections.title: 40-61 A SCENE FROM THE SCENES OF PARADISE AND AND EXAMPLE OF CONVERSATION FROM A RESIDENT OF PARADISE

translation.text: But Allah's chosen servants (shall be spared this woeful end).
For them awaits a known provision,
a variety of delicious fruits; and they shall be honoured

commentary.text: In this there is also a subtle allusion to the fact that, in Paradise, food will not be meant to replenish the bodily deficiencies through diet, for no deficiency will occur in the body in that eternal life nor will the body demand food for its survival rather food will be purely for pleasure and delight. Also, the food will be of known origin nothing completely unfamiliar, exotic or new.

translation.text: in the Gardens of Bliss.
They will be seated upon couches set face to face;
a cup filled with wine from its springs, will be passed around to them;

commentary.text: Here it has not been mentioned as to who will take these cups of wine round to the dwellers of Paradise. This has been stated at other places.
And there will go round to them young boys, exclusively appointed for their service, who will be as lovely as well-guarded pearls. (Surah At- Toor, 24).
They will be attended by brisk-moving boys who will forever remain boys. If you saw them, you would think they were pearls, scattered. (Surah Ad-Dahr, Ayat 19).

translation.text: white, sparkling (wine), a delight to the drinkers.
There will neither be any harm in it for their body nor will it intoxicate their mind.

commentary.text: The wine of Paradise will be free from the evils that are found in the wine of the world. The wine of the world is bitter in taste and smell, adversely impacting the mind and body. Allah SWT says that the wine of Paradise will give full pleasure and delight, without the ill effects associated with worldly wine.

translation.text: Theirs shall be wide-eyed maidens with bashful, restrained glances,

commentary.text: The women of paradise will be lovely looking with big beautiful, bashful eyes. “Restraining glances”: Restraining their looks from everyone except their husbands.

translation.text: so delicate as the hidden peel under an egg's shell.

commentary.text: Umm Salamah has related from the Prophet (PBUH), that when she asked him about the meaning of this Ayat and he said: ‘The delicacy, elegance, perfection and tenderness of women in Paradise will be like the thin skin which is there between the shell of the egg and its fleshy part’. (Ibn Jarir).

translation.text: Then some of them will turn to others, and will ask each other.

commentary.text: The gathering of the People of Paradise, and the exchange between One of Them and His Counterpart in Hell, and His Gratitude for the Blessings of Allah
People of Heaven will ask each other about the experiences of the world.

translation.text: One of them will say: “I had a companion in the world
who used to say: Are you also one of those who confirm the Truth (of life after death)?
After we are dead and have become all dust and bones shall we still be requited?

commentary.text: That is, are you one of those people who has put their faith in an irrational and impossible thing/feat like life-after-death? Meaning this companion would cast doubts in people's minds.

translation.text: He will say: Do you wish to know where he is now?'
Then he will look downwards, and will see him in the depths of Hell.

commentary.text: When the resident of Paradise looks down to see where his companion on earth is, he will see him in the depths of Hell.

translation.text: He will say to him: By Allah, you almost ruined me.
But for Allah's favour, I should be one of those who have been mustered here.

commentary.text: The believer in Heaven will say: You almost destroyed me by casting doubts in my mind. If it had not been for the blessing and mercy of Allah SWT, I would have be in Hell with you.

translation.text: So, are we not going to die,

commentary.text: The believer in Heaven will ask, 'will we not die?'

translation.text: except for our first death? And shall we suffer no chastisement?'”

commentary.text: The style clearly shows that while speaking to his friend in Hell, the dweller of Paradise suddenly starts talking to himself.  He is engaged in a sort of monologue when he speaks the above three sentences as if to say that he has found himself in a state much better than that he ever expected and imagined.
In the Hereafter there is neither death nor any torment. All troubles and distresses will come to an end and we will be blessed with immortality – in sha Allah.

translation.text: Surely this is the supreme triumph.

commentary.text: ENTERING HEAVEN IS SURELY THE BIGGEST SUCCESS.

translation.text: For such ˹honour˺ all should strive.

commentary.text: Ensuring our Hereafter (Heaven) is what all/majority of our striving/work should be focused upon. Our goal or focus in life should be to continually increase our Iman.
Lesson: We all are striving in life whether it be in our work, our homes, our families etc. But how much of our striving and effort is for our Hereafter? What is your end game?

sections.title: 62-74 A SCENE FROM THE SCENES OF HELL

translation.text: Is this a better hospitality or the tree of al-Zaqqum?

commentary.text: The Tree of Zaqqum and its Companions
Allah SWT asks if paradise is better or Hell?
‘Zaqqum.' is a tree of the cactus species that is bitter in taste, obnoxious in smell and sheds milk like juice when cut or broken. Repulsive in every aspect.

translation.text: We have made this tree a trial for the wrong-doers.

commentary.text: Upon hearing about a tree in Hell, the disbelievers get a new opportunity to taunt the Quran and mock the Prophet (PBUH). They ridicule it saying: A tree will grow in the blazing fire of Hell? Here is yet another strange thing the Prophet has told us.

translation.text: It is a tree that grows in the nethermost part of Hell.
Its spathes are like the heads of satans

commentary.text: This is an imaginative simile, meaning the worst, most vile looking tree. One would not want to go near it let alone eat from it.

translation.text: (The people of Hell) will surely eat of it, filling their bellies with it.

commentary.text: Despite the bitter, horrible tasting, thorny fruit the residents of Hell will have to eat it out of sheer hunger/desperation.

translation.text: Then on top of it they will have a brew of boiling water.

commentary.text: Then in an attempt to quench their thirst they will drink boiling hot water (mixed with puss). But this will only intensify the taste of the bitter fruit.

translation.text: Then their return will be to the same blazing Hell.

commentary.text: This shows that when the dwellers of Hell will be in distress due to hunger and thirst, they will be driven to the side of Hell where there will be the zaqqum trees and the springs of boiling water. When they have eaten and drunk, they will be brought back to Hell.
These Ayat’s describe how harsh Hell will be. May Allah SWT protect us all.

sections.title: 75-82 PROPHET NUH PRAYED AND ALLAH RESPOND TO HIS PRAYERS

translation.text: Noah had called upon Us (earlier). See, how excellent We were in answering him!

commentary.text: Prophets are now being mentioned.
Nuh and His People

Nuh (PBUH) was sent as a Prophet to the first people who committed shirk. This refers to the prayer that the Prophet Nuh (PBUH) made to Allah SWT after his people refused to believe despite being preached to for a very long period of time.
This prayer has been related in Surah Al- Qamar Ayat 10. “He called out to his Lord, saying: I am overcome: take now Thy vengeance.
Lesson: Ask Allah SWT and hold fast to dua. Allah SWT is the best responder or Al Mujib.

translation.text: We delivered him and his household from the great calamity;

commentary.text: Allah SWT heard the prayer of his Prophet Nuh (PBUH) and released him from the severe distress that was being caused to him on account of the continuous opposition and antagonism of his nation/people. However, Nuh (PBUH) wife and son (who did not believe) were not saved.

This also contains a subtle hint that just as Prophet Nuh (PBUH) and his companions were saved from the great distress, thus will Allah SWT also ultimately save Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his companions from the great distress that is being caused to them by the people of Makkah.

translation.text: and made his offspring the only ones to survive,

commentary.text: The entire human race was made extinct and only the Prophet Nuh’s family was allowed to inhabit the earth after that. Therefore Nuh (PBUH) is the second Adam.

translation.text: and We established for him a good name among posterity.
Peace be upon Noah among all the nations.

commentary.text: Peace, Salam and praise for Prophet Nuh from Allah SWT amongst all the believers for all time. Till today the world has been praising and speaking well of Nuh (PBUH) for thousands of years. Allah SWT preserved the good mention of Prophet Nuh till the end of time.

translation.text: Thus do We reward all those who do good.

commentary.text: Allah SWT appreciates ALL those who strive in His way. Aspire for greatness in this world and the next by striving in Allah SWT's way. Similar to the prayer of Prophet Nuh, Allah SWT responds to all those who do good. Their duas do not go to waste.
Lesson: Strive in the way of Allah SWT and then expect nothing but goodness, in sha Allah.

sections.title: 83-98 STORY OF PROPHET IBRAHIM, "THE FRIEND OF ALLAH"

translation.text: Ibrahim was on the self-same way (as Nuh)
When he came to his Lord with a pure heart

commentary.text: The Story of Ibrahim and His People
Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) like Prophet Nuh (PBUH) turned to his Raab sincerely and exclusively.

“With a sound heart," سَلِيمٍ قَلْبٍ or Qalb-e-Saleem or Fiitra-e-Saleema has been mentioned twice in the Quran both times for Prophet Ibrahim. It means a heart that was free from all kinds of moral evils, inclinations and desires and free from shirk or doubt. A heart that neither cherishes any malice, jealousy or ill-will against anyone, nor had any evil intention. Thus, a heart that is strong in Iman/faith and firm in character.
We are all created with a pure heart (born on fitra) but then our hearts get corrupted by desires and by doubt.

translation.text: and said to his father and his people: “Whom do you worship?

commentary.text: Prophet Ibrahim did not blindly follow his forefathers but asked incredulously: How and why are you worshiping these false gods?

For further details of this story of the Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH), see (Surah Al-Anaam,Ayats 72-90); (Surah Maryam, Ayats 41-60); (Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayats 51-75); (Surah Ash-Shuara, Ayats 69-89); (Surah Al- Ankabut, Ayats 16-17)

translation.text: Is it false deities that you want to serve rather than Allah?
What do you think of the Lord of the whole Universe?”

commentary.text: Ibrahim (PBUH) continued to question his father and his people. Why have you formed such a wrong view of Allah SWT? Do you think that the gods that you yourselves have carved out from wood and stone can be like Him, or can be His associates in his attributes and rights? Or are you involved in the misunderstanding that you will somehow manage to escape His punishment after you have indulged in such irreverence?

translation.text: So turning their backs, they went away from him.

commentary.text: It appears that the people might be going to some festival of theirs. The family of the Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) might have also asked him to accompany them. He might have excused himself, saying that he was indisposed or about to become sick, therefore, could not go.

translation.text: Then he went quietly to the (temple of the deities) and said: “What is the matter with you, why do you not eat?

commentary.text: There were different kinds of food placed before the idols in the temple.

translation.text: What is the matter with you, why do you not speak?”
Then he turned upon them, striking them with his right hand,
whereupon people came to him running.

commentary.text: Here the story has been told in brief. According to the details given in Surah Al-Anbiya, when they returned from the festival and found all their idols broken to pieces in the temple, they started making investigations. Some people said that a young man called Ibrahim, had been talking against idol-worship. A group of people went running to him and brought him before the multitude.

translation.text: Ibrahim said to them: “Do you worship what you yourselves have carved with your own hands
when it is Allah Who created you and whatever you do?”
They spoke among themselves: “Build him a pyre and then throw him into the furnace.”
They had contrived an evil plan against him, but We abased them all.

commentary.text: Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) was thrown into the fire then Allah SWT rescued him from it safe and sound.
We commanded: O fire, be cool and become safe for Ibrahim. ( Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayat 69)
Then Allah saved him from the fire.  Surah Al-Ankbut, Ayat 24):
People can plot and plan all they want but it is only by Allah SWT's permission that anything good or bad happens – so never ever fear people but fear Allah SWT.

The object of relating this incident is also to warn the people of the Quraish. The way that you have adopted is not the way of the Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH), whose descendants you claim yourselves to be. In fact, his way (Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH), is the path being presented by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). Now, if you plot against him in order to defeat him and frustrate his mission, as the people of the Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) had done against him, you alone will be defeated in the end, because you cannot defeat Muhammad (PBUH).

sections.title: 99-113 PROPHET IBRAHIM WAS ASKED TO OFFER HIS ONLY SON IN SACRIFICE AS A TEST AND HE FULFILLED IT

translation.text: Ibrahim said: “I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.

commentary.text: Ibrahim's Emigration, the Test of the Sacrifice of Isma`il, and how Allah blessed Him
Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) said these (above) words on his departure after he had been delivered safe from the fire and had decided to leave the country.

It means: I am leaving my home and my country for the sake of Allah SWT. My people have turned hostile to me only because of my turning to Him exclusively; otherwise, there was no worldly dispute between them and me because of which I might have had to leave my country. Moreover, I have no place of refuge in the world, to which I may turn. I am leaving my home with full faith and trust only in Allah: I shall go wherever He leads me.
FYI – Prophet Ibrahim was the first to do Hijrat.

translation.text: Lord, grant me a righteous son.”

commentary.text: This prayer/dua shows that Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) at that time was childless. From the details given at other places in the Quran, it becomes clear that he had left his country with only his wife and one nephew (Prophet Lut). Therefore, he naturally desired that Allah SWT should bless him with a righteous child who could be a source of comfort and consolation for him in a foreign land.
LESSON: WHEN ASKING FOR A CHILD ALWAYS ASK ALLAH SWT FOR A RIGHTEOUS CHILD.
FYI --The dua of Prophet Ibrahim was not answered right away but after many years. Allah SWT answers our duas when it is best for us so never stop making dua and never stop hoping for the best.

translation.text: (In response to this prayer) We gave him the good news of a patient son;

arabic_lines: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ السَّعۡىَ قَالَ يٰبُنَىَّ اِنِّىۡۤ اَرٰى فِى الۡمَنَامِ اَنِّىۡۤ اَذۡبَحُكَ فَانْظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرٰىؕ قَالَ يٰۤاَبَتِ افۡعَلۡ مَا تُسَتَجِدُنِىۡۤ اِنۡ شَآءَ اللّٰهُ مِنَ الصّٰبِرِيۡنَ

translation.text: Then when the boy reached the age to work with him, Ibrahim said, “O my dear son! I have seen in a dream that I ˹must˺ sacrifice you. So tell me what you think.” He replied, “O my dear father! Do as you are commanded. Allah willing, you will find me steadfast.”

commentary.text: One should note that Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) had dreamed that he was sacrificing his son (Ismail) and not that he had sacrificed him. Although at that time he understood the dream to mean that he should sacrifice his son thus he was ready to sacrifice him, yet the fine point that Allah had in view in making him see the dream has been explained by Himself in Ayat 105, see below.

Lesson: Prophet Ibrahim consulted and took his son into confidence regarding the dream. He did not just give him an ultimatum and order him. Thus, he allowed his son to think. And indeed what a beautiful response from Ismail (PBUH) who knew that this dream was from Allah SWT.

translation.text: When both surrendered (to Allah's command) and Ibrahim flung the son down on his forehead

commentary.text: Both surrendered: (i) one life (ii) one love/patience. Both submitted to Allah SWT.

translation.text: We cried out: “O Ibrahim,

commentary.text: Allah SWT called out to Ibrahim (PBUH). When Allah SWT might have seen that the old father who had a son after long earnest prayers, has become ready to sacrifice him only for His pleasure and approval; and the son also ready to get slaughtered, His infinite Mercy might have been aroused at the sight, and the Master might have felt great love for the father and son. All this can only be imagined. No words would ever describe the scene adequately.

translation.text: you have indeed fulfilled your dream. Thus do We reward the good-doers.”

commentary.text: Allah SWT rewards the good-doers by removing their distress. The actual objective had been fulfilled by both their submission and preparation to sacrifice for the sake of Allah SWT. Allah SWT does not subject the people who adopt the righteous way to trials in order to involve them in distress and suffering just for the sake of it rather these trials are meant to bring out their excellence and to exalt them to high ranks. Only then does Allah SWT deliver them safe and sound from the dilemma in which He placed them for the sake of the trial.

translation.text: This was indeed a plain trial.

commentary.text: Here Allah SWT is congratulating and saying that yes, indeed, this was a very difficult test/trail. The objective was to see if one holds anything of this world dearer than Allah SWT.
Important to note that tests/trials come in the form of good and bad circumstances/situations.

translation.text: And We ransomed him with a mighty sacrifice,

commentary.text: “A great sacrifice”: A ram, as mentioned in the Bible and the Islamic traditions that Allah SWT's angel presented a ram before the Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) so that he should sacrifice it instead of his son.

Allah SWT made it a tradition till the Day of Resurrection that all the believers should offer an animal sacrifice on the same date so as to keep fresh the memory of the great and unique event signifying true faithfulness and devotion.

translation.text: and We preserved for him a good name among posterity.
Peace be upon Ibrahim.
Thus do We reward the good-doers.
Surely he was one of Our believing servants.
And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a Prophet and among the righteous ones.
And We blessed him and Isaac. Among the offspring of the two some did good and some plainly wronged themselves.

commentary.text: Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) name is mentioned with honor for all generations and for all time. And he was rewarded with another son who was also give Prophethood.
Lesson: With great tests and sacrifice comes great rewards. Question: What are you willing to sacrifice for Allah SWT? Time, money, effort?

sections.title: 114-122 ALLAH BESTOWED HIS FAVORS ON PROPHETS MUSA AND HAROON

translation.text: Verily We bestowed Our favours on Musa and Aaron
and We delivered both of them and their people from the great calamity.

commentary.text: “A great distress”: the huge distress in which they were involved at the hands of Pharaoh and his people.

translation.text: We succoured them, and they gained the upper hand (against their enemies).

commentary.text: Allah SWT granted them with success and victory.

translation.text: We granted them a Clear Book,

commentary.text: Allah SWT blessed them with guidance. Torah is a very clear written scripture: The Ten Commandments.

translation.text: and showed them the Straight Way,
and preserved for them a good name among posterity.

commentary.text: Allah SWT preserved their names (Musa and Haroon Peace Be Upon Them) with honorable mention for all generations and all time.

translation.text: Peace be upon Musa and Aaron.
Thus do We reward the good-doers.
Surely both of them were among Our believing servants.

commentary.text: Peace be upon Musa and Haroon both righteous servants of Allah SWT. And thus does Allah SWT reward ALL his righteous slaves.

sections.title: 123-130 ILYAS (IIYAS) WAS ONE OF THE RASOOLS OF ALLAH

translation.text: Surely, IIyas too was among the Messengers.

commentary.text: Ilyas
Prophet Illya (PBUH) was from among the Israelite Prophets. He has been mentioned only twice in the Quran, here and in Surah Al-Anaam, Ayat 85.

translation.text: (Call to mind) when he said to his people: “Will you not fear Allah?
Do you call upon Baal and forsake the Best of the Creators?
Allah is your Lord and the Lord of your ancestors of yore.”

commentary.text: Message of Prophet Illyas was very clear: Despite idol worship being very common and prevalent it is not acceptable.
In the ancient times, 'Baal,' meant deity or lord; the disbelievers had even given the name of Baal to a special god.

translation.text: But they denounced him as a liar, so they will surely be arraigned (for punishment),
except Allah's chosen servants.

commentary.text: Those who returned to Tawhid and renounced idol worship were saved. They rest were punished.

translation.text: We preserved a good name for him among posterity.
Peace be upon IIyas.

commentary.text: Allah SWT preserved the good mention of Prophet Illyas till the end of time.

sections.title: 131-138 LUT WAS ALSO A RASOOL OF ALLAH

intro.text: The Destruction of the People of Lut (Lot)

translation.text: And Lut too was one of the Messengers.
(Call to mind) when We delivered him and all his kinsfolk,
except for an old woman who was among those that stayed behind.

commentary.text: This implies the wife of the Prophet Lut (PBUH) who did not migrate with her husband but remained behind with her people and was punished.

translation.text: Then We utterly destroyed the rest of them.
You pass by their desolate habitations in the morning
and at night. Do you still not understand?

commentary.text: The reference is to the exhumed habitations of the people of Lut that the Quraishite merchants passed day and night during their trade journeys to Syria and Palestine.
Lesson: Reflect!

sections.title: 139-148 STORY OF PROPHET YUNUS (JOHAN)

translation.text: And Yunus too was one of the Messengers.

commentary.text: The Story of Yunus

This is the third place where the Prophet Yunus (PBUH) has been mentioned in the Quran. Before this he has already been mentioned in Surah Yunus and Surah Al-Anbiya. (For reference, please see (Surah Younus, Ayat 98 ) and (Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayats 87-88)

translation.text: Call to mind when he fled to the laden ship,

commentary.text: The Quran does not mention where Prophet Yunus’s people lived, but it is understood that they were not far from the sea. Reports tell us that Prophet Yunus was frustrated by his people’s continued denial of his message. He warned them against God’s impending punishment and then abandoned them in anger. His anger led him to the sea-shore where he boarded an overloaded or laden ship.

translation.text: cast lots, and was among the losers.

commentary.text: When the ship was in the middle of the ocean, it was hit by a raging storm. It was widely believed, at that time, that such a disaster meant that among the passengers there must be someone who had incurred God’s anger. For the ship to withstand the storm that person had to be thrown overboard. They, thus, drew lots and Yunus (PBUH) was the one who lost (three times).  Although they knew him to be a virtuous and God-fearing man, the drawing of his lot was confirmed. Therefore, they threw him into the sea or he might have jumped himself.

translation.text: Then a fish swallowed him, and he was blameworthy

commentary.text: He was then swallowed by the whale. 'Deserving of blame,' because he abandoned the assignment Allah SWT had given him, leaving his people in anger before seeking God’s permission. When he felt acute distress inside the whale’s belly, he glorified God and prayed for His forgiveness, stating that he had wronged himself. He said in his prayer: “There is no deity other than You! Limitless are You in Your glory! I have done wrong indeed!” (21: 87)
The Arabic word, 'Muleem,' means someone who is worthy of blame because of his sin and error, whether anyone else blames him or not. (Ibn Jarir).

translation.text: Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah,

commentary.text: This Ayat has two meanings and both are implied: (1) That Prophet Yunus (PBUH) was not heedless of Allah SWT but of those who glorify and adore Allah SWT constantly and perpetually (2) That when he was inside the whale he turned to Allah SWT alone and glorified Him. (Ayat e Kareema.)
Lesson: Good words ascend to Allah SWT. Always have good expectations and hope in Allah SWT and in His infinite Mercy.

translation.text: he would certainly have remained in its belly till the Day of Resurrection.

commentary.text: The surah makes it clear that, 'had he not been of those who truly glorified God, he would have stayed in the whale's belly till the Day of Resurrection'. This does not mean that the fish would have lived till Resurrection and the Prophet Yunus (PBUH) would have remained alive in its belly till then but that the fish’s belly would have become his grave till Resurrection.

translation.text: But We threw him on a wide bare tract of land while he was ill

commentary.text: That is, when Prophet Yunus (PBUH) confessed his fault and began to glorify Allah SWT like a true and sincere believer, the fish spat him up on the beach by Allah SWT's command. Allah SWT answered Prophet Yunus dua and delivered him from distress.
The beach was a bare plain, without any vegetation on it, or anything to provide him shade or any means of food.

translation.text: and caused a gourd tree to grow over him,

commentary.text: When he was cast out of the whale, he was both sick and naked. Therefore Allah SWT, 'caused a gourd tree to grow over him.' Its broad leaves covering him, and protected him against flies, which are said not to come near this plant. This was part of the favour Allah SWT bestowed upon Prophet Yunus that he was cured, nourished and given shelter. Lesson: Turn to Allah SWT and He will fully take care of you and all your needs.

The Arabic word 'Yaqteen,' means a tree which does not stand on a stem but grows and spreads like a creeper, e.g. a pumpkin, cucumber, water-melon, etc. A creeper was produced miraculously, so that its leaves provided shade to Prophet Yunus and its fruit served him both as food and as shade/shelter.

translation.text: and We sent him forth to a nation of a hundred thousand or more,

commentary.text: When he recovered, Allah SWT returned him to the people whom he had left in anger. In turn, they believed and prayed for God’s forgiveness. Allah SWT thus accepted their repentance, sparing them the punishment He inflicts on people who deny His message:
Lesson: Remember Allah SWT in good times and Allah SWT will remember you in bad times.
When we turn to Allah SWT (with full trust/tawakkul) then He fully takes care of us.

sections.title: 149-166 MUSHRIK'S CLAIM OF ANGELS BEING DAUGHTERS OF ALLAH AND JINNS HAVING BLOOD RELATIONS WITH ALLAH ARE UTTERLY FALSE

translation.text: So ask their opinion: “(Are you convinced) that your Lord should have daughters and you should have sons?

commentary.text: Refutation of Those Who attribute Children to Allah and say that the Angels are His Daughters
Allah SWT denounces those who attribute daughters to Him and ascribe to themselves what they desire, i.e., male offspring.

A theme that started from ayat 1 is continued from here. Traditions show that in Arabia the tribes of Quraish, Juhainah, Bani Salimah, Khuzaah, Bani Mulaih, etc. held the belief that the angels were Allah SWT's daughters. This ignorance has been referred to at several places in the Quran, e.g. in (Surah An-Nisa, Ayat 117); (Surah An- Nahl, Aytas 57-58); (Surah Bani-Israil, Ayat 40); (Surah Az- Zukhruf, Ayats 16, 19); (Surah An-Najm, Ayats 21-27).

translation.text: Did We create the angels as females the while they witnessed?”

commentary.text: FYI – Angels are made/created out of light.

translation.text: Behold, it is one of their fabrications that they say:
“Allah has begotten.” They are liars!

commentary.text: They say Allah SWT has a child. Indeed they are liars!

translation.text: Did He choose daughters rather than sons?
What is the matter with you that you make such strange judgements?
Will you then not take heed?
Do you have any clear authority for such claims?
Bring your Book, if you are truthful.

commentary.text: There can be only two bases for regarding angels as the daughters of Allah SWT. Either such a thing could be said on the basis of observation or the one who asserted it should possess a divine book in which Allah SWT Himself stated that the angels were His daughters.

However, if those who held this belief can neither make a claim to have observed such a thing nor do they possess any divine book containing this assertion then there could be no greater stupidity than to base this religious belief on mere conjecture.

translation.text: They have established a kinship between Allah and the angels; and the angels know well that these people will be arraigned (as culprits).

commentary.text: These people (disbelievers) created a lineage between Allah SWT and Jinns. More lies!

translation.text: [The angels say], ‘Every single one of us has his appointed place:

commentary.text: Angels say: Forget about being Allah SWT's children, we do not even have the power to exceed in any way or degree the place, position and status appointed for each of us by Allah SWT.  Each one has their own place in the Heavens and in the places of worship that we cannot overstep.
Hadith: A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said, "The Messenger of Allah said: There is no place in the lower Heaven without an angel standing or prostrating in it.

translation.text: Verily we range ourselves in rows (as humble servants)

commentary.text: Also see (37:1)
Going back to the beginning of the surah – (37:1) 'By those who range themselves in row.'

The angels refute the superstition that they are the daughters of Allah SWT, making it clear that each one of them has their own status/position that they do not exceed. They are a type of God’s creation who worship Him alone. They are assigned certain tasks and they fulfill them, ranging themselves in rows for prayer and extolling God’s glory.

Abu Nadrah said, "When the Iqamah had been given, Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would turn to face the people and say:`Make your rows straight, for Allah wants you to follow the ways of the angels.'
Then he would say: And verily, we range ourselves/stand in rows.

translation.text: and we are of those who glorify Allah.”

commentary.text: Means: we (angels) stand in rows and glorify the Lord, praising Him, sanctifying Him and declaring Him to be above any faults or shortcomings. We are servants of Him and in need of Him, humbling ourselves before Him.'

sections.title: 167-182 ALLAH HAS PROMISED TO HELP HIS RASOOLS AND HIS DEVOTEES

translation.text: We have already given Our promise to Our Messengers
that they would surely be helped,
and that Our forces will certainly prevail.

commentary.text: This is a Makki surah thus a source of comfort for the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) who was suffering grave persecution at the hands of the mushriqeen of Arabia. Allah SWT says, don’t worry, right now the situation may be bleak but success is yours. This has been decreed and will happen in this lifetime.
The truths preached by the Prophets of Allah SWT, for thousands of years, have been unalterable till today. No one has been able to disprove them in any way.

translation.text: So, (O Prophet), leave them alone for a while,
and see, and soon they too shall see.

commentary.text: It will not take long when they (disbelievers) will see their defeat and your victory with their own eyes. This proved to be true. Hardly 14 to 15 years had passed after the revelation of these Ayats when the pagans of Makkah witnessed the Prophet (PBUH) enter their city as a conqueror and then a few years later the same people saw that Islam had overwhelmed not only Arabia but the mighty empires of Rome and Iran as well.

arabic_lines: سُبۡحٰنَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ الۡعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُوۡنَ

translation.text: Exalted be your Lord, the Lord of Glory, above what they attribute to Him,

commentary.text: Allah SWT is perfect and above all descriptions that people invent i.e that Allah SWT has a son or daughter.

translation.text: and all praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Universe.

commentary.text: ALL Praise and ALL Gratitude is for Allah SWT, the Lord of the Universe.

items.text: This surah is a Makki surah therefore the key themes are Tawhid, Prophet hood and the Hereafter. Shirk is the first theme, then a vivid description of Heaven and Hell is mentioned. After this the Prophets are discussed. Lastly the theme of shirk is again reiterated (that is that the angels are not Allah SWT daughters and the Jinn have no blood lineage with Allah SWT.)
ETIQUETTE OF DUA:
All Prophets made dua to Allah SWT, i.e. Prophets Nuh for his nation, Ibrahim for son, Younus for being saved from the belly of the fish, Musa when he went to the Paraoh, etc.
Ask again and again. Do not be shy of asking. Mention state of neediness.
Make dua with sincerity, conviction, full Iman/faith and from the depth of your heart.
Make dua using Allah SWT’s names for example, Al Ghafaar (most forgiving).
Send blessings upon the Prophet (PBUH) before and after making dua.
Mention your good deeds when making dua.
Before dua perform some good deeds (salah, fast, charity etc.) because good deeds make good words ascend towards our Raab.
FORBIDDEN IN ISLAM
Superstations, soothsayers, fortune tellers are all forbidden in Islam. Only Allah SWT has the knowledge of the unseen.
ALLAH SWT’S REWARD

When we do something/anything for Allah SWT (to earn His pleasure and goodwill) then the reward is beyond our expectation because Allah SWT is most Appreciative and All Thankful (Al Shakoor). For example, the Prophet’s endeavors it is good mention for all of eternity.
So, surpass others and complete in doing good deeds. Iman + good deeds = Success
Lesson: you give Allah a bit and He will give you much much more that you ever could expect.
