front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the alphabetic letter Şāad with which it begins.

items.text: صٓ وَالۡقُرۡاٰنِ ذِى الذِّكۡرِؕ
(38:1) Sad, and by the Qur'an full of reminders!

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makki Surah.  It was revealed around the time of first Hijrah to Ebyssinia about the 5th year of Prophethood.  It has 88 Ayats in 5 Rukus. This Surah was sent down in the period when the Holy Prophet had started openly calling the people towards Islam causing great alarm and fear among the chiefs of the Quraysh. They openly and aggressively were attacking the Prophet (PBUH) personally and his message.

front_matter.label: Historical Background
front_matter.text:
When Abu Talib fell ill, and the Quraysh chiefs knew that his end was near, they decided to approach the old chief with the request that he should solve the dispute between them and his nephew. For they feared that if Abu Talib died and then they subjected Muhammad (upon whom be Allah's peace) to a harsh treatment, after his death, the Arabs would taunt them, saying, "They were afraid of the old chief as long as he lived now that he is dead, they have started maltreating his nephew."

At least 25 of the Quraysh chiefs including Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan, Umayyah bin Khalaf, As bin Wa'il, Aswad bin al-Muttalib, 'Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ait, Utbah and Shaibah went to Abu Talib. They put before him their complaints against the Holy Prophet.

Abu Talib called the Holy Prophet and asked him why he was insulting the gods of the Quraysh.

The Holy Prophet replied, "Dear uncle: I shall request them to agree upon a thing which, if they accept, will enable them to conquer the whole of Arabia and subject the non-Arab world to their domination. Then Holy Prophet said: La ilaha ill-Allah. At this the chiefs got up and left.

front_matter.label: Subject and Topics
front_matter.text:
The central theme of this Surah is Tawhid. The Surah begins with a review of the aforesaid meeting. Making the dialogue between the Holy Prophet and the disbelievers the basis, Allah SWT says that the actual reason for their denial is not any defect in the message of Islam but their own arrogance, jealousy and insistence on blindly following their ancestors.

For them the concept of Tawhid and the Hereafter is not only an unacceptable impossibility but also a concept that only deserves to be ridiculed and mocked.

Allah SWT in the initial part of the Surah and in its last sentences has warned the disbelievers that: The man whom you are ridiculing today and whose guidance you reject will soon overpower you, and the time is not far when in this very city of Makkah, where you are persecuting him, he will overwhelm you completely.

Describing nine Prophets, one after the other and then with greater detail the story of the Prophets Dawud and Suleiman (PBU them); Allah SWT has emphasized that His Law of Justice is impartial and objective and that He calls to account and punishes every wrongdoer whomever they may be. That He likes only those people who do not persist in wrongdoing but repent as soon as they are warned and pass their life in the world keeping in mind their accountability in the Hereafter.

After this, the final end that the obedient servants and the disobedient people will meet in the Hereafter, has been depicted, and two things have been especially impressed on the disbelievers:(1) That the leaders and guides whom the ignorant people are following blindly in the world, on the way of deviation, will have reached Hell even before their followers in the Hereafter, and the two groups will be cursing each other there; and (2) that the disbelievers will be amazed to see that there is no trace whatever in Hell of the believers whom they used to regard as contemptible in the world.

In conclusion, mention has been made of the story of Adam and Iblis/satan, which is meant to tell the disbelieving Quraysh that the same arrogance and vanity which was preventing them from bowing before Muhammad (PBUH) had prevented Iblis/satan also from bowing before Adam. Iblis/satan felt jealous of the high rank God had given to Adam and became accursed when he disobeyed His Command. Likewise, "You, O people of Quraysh, are feeling jealous of the high rank God has bestowed on Muhammad (PBUH) and are not prepared to obey him whom God has appointed His messenger. Therefore, you will be doomed ultimately to the same fate as will be met by Satan."

sections.title: 1-14 AL-QURAN IS FULL OF ADMONITION UNBELIEVERS ARE IN SHEER ARROGANCE FOR CALLING THE PROPHET AS LIARS

translation.text: Sad, and by the Qur'an full of reminders!

commentary.text: The letter Şāad is a single disjointed letter therefore cannot be a separate Ayat.

Allah SWT states an oath by the letter Şāad صٓand by the Qurān, which He describes here as a reminder (of our purpose in life), full of admonition and advice. The words dhidh-dhikr, can have two meanings: (1) Dhi sharaf: the noble Quran. (2) Dhi at-tadhkir: the Quran that is full of admonition/warning/caution or the Quran that serves as a reminder to arouse the heedless.

translation.text: Nay, but the unbelievers are steeped in arrogance and stubborn defiance.

commentary.text: The answer to the oath is omitted, the Ayat begins with the word, ‘but’, which suggests that there is a move away from the initial subject matter: the oath by the letter Şāad and the Qur’ān. The oath sounds incomplete because what it intends to affirm is not mentioned.

The reason for the denial of these disbelievers is not that the religion that is being presented before them is unsound, or that Muhammad (PBUH) has shown some slackness in presenting the truth before them, rather their own boasting and bragging, their haughtiness and stubbornness.

translation.text: How many a nation did We destroy before them! (When they approached their doom) they cried out (for deliverance), but the time for deliverance was already past.
They wondered that a warner had come to them from among themselves, and the deniers of the Truth said: “This is a sorcerer, and a big liar.

commentary.text: They are so foolish that when a man from their own kind/ clan and brotherhood, whom they knew well, was appointed to warn them, they questioned/mistrusted him, whereas if some other kind of creature had been sent down from heaven to warn human being or an utter stranger had arisen from among them and started functioning as a prophet then that would have been strange.

The disbelievers used the word 'sahir' (wizard, sorcerer, magician) awho is a liar for the Prophet (PBUH) in the sense that whoever came in contact with him was so influenced by him that he would become a devout follower like a person possessed. He would least mind severing of his connections with others or incurring material losses. The father would give up the son and the son would give up the father. The wife would separate from the husband and the husband would separate from the wife. One would at once be prepared to leave his country if so required. (For further details, see (Surah Al- Anbiya, Ayat 3)

translation.text: Has he made the gods one single God? This is truly astounding.”

commentary.text: The Mushirks found the concept of Tawhid very strange. They said that no one could remain content with One God only. From one deity the Mushirks would ask for children and from another the provisions of life, and from yet another whatever they prayed for. Now this man is telling us that all worship and gratitude belongs only to Allah SWT? Tawhid is the central theme of this surah.

translation.text: The chiefs among them went forth saying, “Carry on, and stand firm in devotion to your gods. Certainly this is just a scheme ˹for power˺.

commentary.text: The reference is to the chiefs who got up and left Abu Talib when they had heard what the Prophet (PBUH) said. They felt that the Prophet’s (PBUH) asking them to affirm faith in “La-ilaha ill-Allah” was only so as to overpower both Arabia and the adjoining lands.
The Reason for the Revelation of These Ayat

When Abu Talib fell sick, some people of the Quraysh, including Abu Jahl, called upon him and said, `Your brother's son is insulting our gods; he does such and such and says such and such. Why don't you send for him and tell him not to do that?'
Abu Talib said to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), `O son of my brother, why are your people complaining about you and claiming that you insult their gods and say such and such?'
The Prophet (PBUH) said, 'O uncle, all I want from them is one word which, if they say it, the Arabs will become their followers and the non-Arabs will pay Jizyah to them.'
Abu Talib said, `What word is it? O son of my brother.'
The Prophet (PBUH) said, “La-ilaha ill-Allah”
The people of the Quraysh stood up in agitation, saying, 'Has he made the gods into One God. Verily, this is a curious thing!'
Then these Ayats were revealed.

translation.text: Their armed alliance is weak and will be crushed.

commentary.text: “Their” implies the city of Makkah and the people of Quraysh. That is, the time is approaching when these people shall be humbled and overwhelmed in the very place where they are opposing and mocking the Prophet (PBUH). Soon they will be standing, with heads hung down, before the same man whom they despise and refuse to recognize as a Prophet of Allah SWT.

translation.text: Before them the people of Noah, Ad, and Pharoh of the tent-pegs gave the lie (to the Messengers)

commentary.text: A Reminder of Those Who were destroyed among the Previous Nations

Allah SWT tells us about past nations and the punishment/vengeance that struck them for their going against the Messengers and disbelieving in the Prophets, (peace be upon them). We have already seen their stories in detail in numerous places in the Quran.

The use of dhul-autad (tent-pegs) for Pharoh is either in the sense that his kingdom was very strong as though a stake firmly driven into the ground or that wherever his large armies camped, pegs of the tents were seen driven into the ground on every side.

translation.text: and so did Thamud and the people of Lot and the people of Aykah. These were all leagued together.
Each of them gave the lie to Messengers and My decree of chastisement came upon them.

commentary.text: They all rejected the messengers and thus they were deservedly struck by punishment.

sections.title: 15-26 STORY OF PROPHET DAWUD -MOUNTAINS AND BIRDS USED TO SING THE RHYMES OF ALLAH AND STORY OF THE TWO LITIGANTS WHO CAME TO DAWUD FOR A DECISION

translation.text: They say: “Our Lord, hasten to us our share (of chastisement) before the Day of Reckoning.”

commentary.text: Disbelievers, in their extreme denial, were asking Allah SWT to hasten the Day of Reckoning that the Prophet (PBUH) was threatening them with. They said: ‘Whatever punishment is to be inflicted on us should be inflicted immediately.'

translation.text: (O Prophet), bear with patience what they say, and call to mind Our servant Dawud, who was endowed with great strength and who constantly turned (to Allah).

commentary.text: Allah SWT tells us about His servant and Messenger Dawud, (peace be upon him)

The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is being comforted by Allah SWT and told to have patience and ignore the disbelievers of Makkah for calling him a sorcerer, a liar and their accusation that he has vested interest in preaching the doctrine of Tawhid i.e. political aspirations of capturing Arabia.

The example of Prophet Dawud, (PBUH) is given who possessed strength in worship coupled with the proper understanding of Islam. He possessed great powers including; (i) physical strength that he displayed during his combat against Goliath, (ii) military and political supremacy by which he crushed the neighboring idolatrous nations and established a strong Islamic empire, (iii) moral strength by which he ruled like a poor king and always feared Allah SWT and the bounds set by Him, and the (iv) power of worship by virtue of which, in addition to governing and fighting in the cause of Allah SWT, he fasted every alternate day and spent a third of the night in worship. Imam Bukhari has related, on the authority of Abu- Darda, that whenever Prophet Dawud (PBUH) was mentioned, the Prophet (PBUH) used to say: ‘He was the greatest worshiper of God.’

Dawud (PBUH), used to sleep for half of the night, stand in prayer for a third of the night, then sleep for a sixth of the night.  He used to fast alternate days. He never fled from the battlefield, and he always turned to Allah SWT.

(For the story of the prophet Dawud (peace be upon him), see (Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayat 251); (Surah Bani-Israil, Ayat 55); (Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayats 78-81); (Surah An-Naml, Ayat 15) , and (E.Ns 14 to 16 of Surah Saba).

translation.text: With him We had subjected the mountains that they join him in celebrating Allah's glory, evening and morning,
and the birds, too, in their flocks, and turn again and again to celebrating Allah's glory.

commentary.text: For explanation, see ( Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayat 79).

translation.text: And We strengthened his kingdom and endowed him with wisdom and decisive judgement.

commentary.text: Prophet Dawud, (PBUH) was clear, eloquent and direct in his speech and able to extract the basic/core points from any argument/discussion so as to precisely determine the real issue and pass a decisive judgment.  He was granted wisdom, understanding and mastery of language of the highest degree.

translation.text: Has the story of the litigants reached you of those who entered his private chambers by climbing over the wall?

commentary.text: The Story of the Two Litigants

Mentioning Prophet Dawud's sterling qualities in the introduction was only to point out the high caliber of the character with whom this incident took place. Note: Prophets are above making big mistakes. Yet, small mistakes in judgment can be made and then the importance of repentance to Allah SWT.

translation.text: As they came upon Dawud and he was frightened of them, they said: “Be not afraid. We are just two litigants: one of us has committed excess against the other. So judge rightly between us, and be not unjust; and guide us to the Right Way.

commentary.text: Prophet Dawud, (PBUH) was alarmed because the two men had appeared in the private quarters of the ruler of the land suddenly, by climbing over the wall, instead of going before him by the proper entrance.

translation.text: Behold, this is my brother; he has ninety-nine ewes and I have only one ewe.” And yet he said: “Give her into my charge,” and he got the better of me in argument.

commentary.text: “Brother” does not mean a real brother but a brother- in- faith and a member of one’s own clan.

One should note that the complainant did not say that the other person had taken away his only sheep and added it to his own sheep, but said that he was asking for it, and since he was a powerful person, he (the complainant) being a weak and poor man could not reject his demand and was getting pressurized.

translation.text: Dawud said: “He has certainly wronged you in seeking to add your ewe to his ewes; and indeed many who live together commit excesses, one to the other, except those that believe and act righteously; and they are but few.” (While so saying) Dawud realized that it is We Who have put him to test; therefore, he sought the forgiveness of his Lord, and fell down, bowing and penitently turning (to Him).

commentary.text: THIS AYAT IS A SAJDAH TILAWAT – Prostration here is mandatory
Prophet Dawud (PBUH) gave a hasty decision after hearing only what one party had to say and ruled in favor of the complainant.
Iman                            +                righteous deeds = Success.
(Allah consciousness) + (when giving is our focus) prevent us from oppressing others that leads to success.

The two men disappeared. In fact, they were two angels. They had come to test Dawud, the prophet God regarding his fairness before passing judgment. They had put the case to him in a very sentimental way, one that invited immediate sympathy. However, a judge must not allow sentiment to take charge. He must not be hasty. Above all, he must not rely on the statement of only one party, without allowing the other party to present his case and submit his evidence. In other words, appearances can often be deceptive or incomplete.
At this point Dawud realized that this was a test and he fell down in prostration and again turned to God in repentance.
Lesson: To err is human. However, our reaction after the mistake defines us, that is, our we arrogant/defiant in our attitude or do we immediately and humbly turn to Allah SWT in repentance.
Upon making a mistake and realizing our shortcoming we should repent (without delay) and offer 2 rakat salat.

translation.text: Thereupon We forgave him his shortcoming and indeed (an exalted position of) nearness awaits him, and an excellent resort.

commentary.text: Prophet Dawud (PBUH) had certainly committed an error, but the nature of the error was not such as could not be forgiven, or if forgiven, it would have deposed him from his high rank. Allah SWT Himself says: ‘When he fell down prostrate and repented, he was not only forgiven but his high rank in the world and the Hereafter also remained unaffected.’
Lesson: Mistakes can bring us closer to Allah SWT – so prostrate in repentance and gratitude.

translation.text: (We said to him): “O Dawud, We have appointed you vicegerent on earth. Therefore, rule among people with justice and do not follow (your) desire lest it should lead you astray from Allah's Path. Allah's severe chastisement awaits those who stray away from Allah's Path, for they had forgotten the Day of Reckoning.

commentary.text: Advice to Rulers and Leaders and those in a position of authority

This is advice from Allah SWT, to those who are in positions of authority. Judge with the truth and do not follow you desires/whims nor be hasty when dealing with people. There will be severe punishment in store for those who do this.

sections.title: 27-29 ALLAH HAS NOT CREATED THE HEAVENS AND THE EARTH IN VAIN

translation.text: We did not create this heaven and earth and all that lies between them in vain. That is the fancy of those who denied the Truth. So woe from the Fire to all who deny the Truth.

commentary.text: The Wisdom behind the Creation of This World

Allah SWT tells us that He did not create the creatures in vain; He created them to worship Him Alone, then He will gather them on the Day of Gathering and will reward the obedient and punish the disbelievers. Allah SWT has not created anything in the world merely in sport and fun so that it may be without any wisdom, purpose and justice, and there may occur no result from any act, good or bad.

This is the conclusion of the preceding discourse as well as an introduction to the following theme. The object of this statement as a conclusion to the discourse is to impress the following truth: Man has not been left to wander about at will in the world nor is this world a lawless kingdom that one may do here whatever he likes with impunity.

As an introduction to the following theme: The person who does not believe in rewards and punishments, and thinks that both good and evil people will ultimately end up in the dust after death and that nobody will be called to account, nor will anyone be rewarded for good or punished for evil, in fact, regards the world as a plaything and its Creator a senseless player.
The same thing has been stated in different ways at several places in the Quran.
Did you think that We created you without any purpose, and that you would never be brought back to Us? (Surah Al-Muminun, Ayat 115).

We have not created the heavens and the earth and whatever lies between them merely in sport: We have created them with the truth, but most of them do not know. For the resurrection of them all the appointed time is the Day of Decision. (Surah Ad-Dukhan, Ayat 38-40).

translation.text: Shall We then treat alike those that believe and act righteously and those that create mischief on earth? Or treat alike the God-fearing and the wicked?

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Iman + good deeds = Success

Do you think it is reasonable and fair that both the pious and the wicked should be treated alike in the end? Do you regard this concept as satisfying that the pious man should not get any reward for his piety and the wrongdoer should not receive any punishment for his sins?

Obviously, if there is to be no Hereafter, no accountability and no reward nor punishment, it negates both Allah SWT’s wisdom and His justice, and the entire order of the Universe becomes a blind order. On this assumption there remains no motive for doing good and no deterrent against evil.

translation.text: This is the Blessed Book that We have revealed to you, (O Muhammad), that people with understanding may reflect over its verses and those with understanding derive a lesson.

commentary.text: The Quran is a Book full of barakah – in Arabic 'barakah,' means something that helps extract blessings/khair from something else. Potentially, we all have khair in us (our fitra/ruh) but more often than not it is dormant and we are not using it to its full potential. The Quran (which is full of barakh) helps extract and develop this khair within us.

Another example of barakah in the Quran has been used for rain; as it nourishes and brings out the best from the dry dirt land. The seeds are rejuvenated and life is given to dry, dead land via rainfall.
The Quran provides the best guidance to improve and reform our lives.

sections.title: 30-40 STORY OF  SULEIMAN 'S INSPECTION OF STEEDS TO BE USED IN JIHAD

translation.text: We bestowed upon Dawud (an illustrious son), Suleiman. How excellent a servant (of Ours he was)! Indeed he constantly turned to Us in devotion.

commentary.text: Dawud was gifted Suleiman (a child is a gift from Allah SWT)

Prophet Suleiman (PBUH) has been mentioned already at the followings places: (Surah Al- Baqarah, Ayat 102); (Surah Bani-Israil, Ayat 5); (Surah Al- Anbiya, Ayats 78-82); (Surah An-Naml, Ayats 15-44); (Surah Saba, Ayats 12-14).

translation.text: And when one evening well-trained and running horses of noble breed were brought to him

commentary.text: Horses were brought for Suleiman (PBUH) so that he could review and inspect his grand cavalry. As the Prophet Suleiman (PBUH) had kept these horses for fighting in the way of Allah SWT, he called them 'khair or the good wealth.'

translation.text: he said: “Lo! I have come to love this wealth on account of the remembrance of my Lord.” And when the horses disappeared,

commentary.text: When a squadron of fine, well-bred horses was presented before Prophet Suleiman (PBUH), he said: ‘I love this wealth not for the sake of personal glory or desire but for the cause of my Lord.’ Then he ordered that the horses run a race, and they disappeared from sight. He ordered that they be brought back, and when they were brought back, according to Ibn Abbas: He started passing his hand on their necks and shanks with love. Missed his Asr prayer.

translation.text: (he ordered): “Bring these horses back to me,” and then he began to gently stroke their shanks and necks.

commentary.text: Prophet Suleiman (PBUH), became so absorbed in reviewing the horses and watching their races, that he forgot to offer his Asr Prayer, or according to some others, to perform certain devotions that he used to perform before the sunset. Then when the sun went down, he commanded that the horses be brought back, and when they came back, the Prophet Suleiman (PBUH) started slashing them with the sword, or in other words, slaughtering them as a sacrifice to Allah SWT, because they had caused him to become heedless of the remembrance of Allah SWT.

translation.text: Surely We put Suleiman to the test and cast upon his throne a mere body. Thereupon he penitently turned (to Us).

commentary.text: Allah SWT says He tested Prophet Suleiman (PBUH), but the nature of the test/fitna is not mentioned (with any certainty). Prophet Suleiman (PBUH) did not say: In sha Allah: if Allah so wills.

As a matter of fact, this is one of the most difficult places of the Quran. Thus, anyone who is careful about what he says cannot give any details of these two incidents with any degree of certainty. All he can say is that Suleiman (PBUH) underwent some test concerning the way he conducted his kingdom’s affairs, just as God tests Prophets to guide them and keep them from error. We also learn that Suleiman (PBUH) turned to his Lord in submission and sought His forgiveness.

translation.text: He said: “My Lord, forgive me and bestow upon me a kingdom such as none other after me will deserve. Surely You are the Bounteous Giver.”

commentary.text: How Allah tested Prophet Suleiman then made Things easy for Him
Prophet Suleiman then prayed for forgiveness with hope and dedication.

The proper interpretation of Suleiman (PBUH)'s request is that he did not ask for something to show that he was the most favored person, but that he asked instead for a special thing so as to distinguish him from any future king and master. It was to be of a special nature and something not normally possessed by kings.

Allah SWT by means of these two stories wants to impress two things simultaneously: (1) Let alone the common men, even high-ranking Prophets were not spared from His strict accountability; and, (2) The right attitude for man is not to brag and feel proud after committing an error, but to bow down humbly before his Lord as soon as he realizes his sin. It was the result of this attitude that Allah SWT not only forgave the mistakes but blessed them with still more favors and kindness.

translation.text: We subjected the wind to him, so that it blew gently at his bidding, wherever he directed it,

commentary.text: God answered Suleiman (PBUH)'s prayer and made the wind subservient to him. For explanation, see (Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayat 81 and E.N. 74). However, there is one thing that requires further explanation here. In Surah Al-Anbiya, where mention has been made of subjecting the wind for Prophet Suleiman (PBUH), it has been described as the strongly blowing wind, but here it is stated: 'it blew by his command gently wherever he intended,' means that the wind in itself was strong and violent as is needed for moving the sailing-ships but it had been made gentle for the Prophet in the sense that it blew however he wanted it to blow for his commercial fleets.

translation.text: and We also subjected the devils to him all kinds of builders and divers;
and others that were bound with chains.

commentary.text: God also made the jinns subservient to him. They built whatever he wished them to build, and they also dived into the sea to bring him whatever he wished. Allah SWT further gave him the authority to punish anyone who disobeyed him or who caused corruption and to chain the rebellious Jinns by their hands and feet, or as he deemed fit or needed. Thus, he was given full authority over whatever favors God granted him. Thus, did God grant Suleiman (PBUH) very extraordinary blessings and favours.

sections.title: 41-48 STORY OF AYUB (JOB), HIS SICKNESS AND RELIEF

translation.text: And remember Our servant Job: when he cried to his Lord: “Behold, Satan has afflicted me with much hardship and suffering.”

commentary.text: This is the fourth place in the Quran where Prophet Ayub (PBUH) has been mentioned. Before this he has been mentioned in (Surah An-Nisa, Ayat 163); (Surah Al-Anaam, Ayat 84 )and (Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayats 83-84).

This does not mean that Satan has afflicted Prophet Ayub (PBUH) with illness and brought distress upon him but it means: The affliction of the severities of illness, the loss of property and wealth, and the desertion of the near and dear ones is not so great a torment and trouble for Prophet Ayub (PBUH) as the temptation of Satan, who is exploiting his condition to despair him of his Lord and wants that he should turn ungrateful to Him and become desperate and impatient. Yet, Prophet Ayub never complained other than that satan is harming me. All bad was attributed to satan out of respect to Allah SWT.
Allah SWT has granted Satan only the power of temptation. He has not given him the power to afflict illness upon the worshipers of Allah SWT and thus compel them to deviate.
Lesson: When making dua mention our state of neediness to Allah SWT as a means of drawing closer to Him.
Rule: Prophets experience hardship the most, then the pious people and then others.

translation.text: (We commanded him): “Stamp your foot on earth, and here is cool water to wash with and to drink.”

commentary.text: As soon as Prophet Ayub (PBUH) stamped his foot on the ground, a spring gushed forth by Allah SWT’s command, drinking from which and washing with which was the remedy of Prophet Ayub (PBUH) disease. Most probably he was suffering from some skin disease. According to the Bible Job or Prophet Ayub (PBUH) was covered in sore boils from the sole of his foot unto the crown of his head.
Lesson: Shifa/cure is in Allah SWT's hands. Adopt means but put your entire trust (tawakul) in Allah SWT.

translation.text: And We granted to him his family and also the like of them, as a mercy from Us, and as a reminder to people of understanding,

commentary.text: Traditions show that during this illness, except his wife, everyone else had deserted Prophet Ayub (PBUH); even his children had turned away. To this Allah SWT has alluded, saying: When We granted him health, the whole family returned to him, and then We granted him even more children.
Prophet Ayub was ill for 18 years. After his cure he became more handsome than before and Allah SWT sent locusts of gold for him (wealth beyond imagination.)

Lesson: Neither should man forget God and become arrogant in good times nor despair of Him in bad times. Good fortune and misfortune are entirely in the Power of Allah SWT, If He wills, He can change the best times of man into the worst times and the worst into the best.
Bad things can happen to good people but never despair as relief is near.

translation.text: And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob they were endowed with great strength and vision.

commentary.text: These Prophets as “men of great power and insight.” They did not live like the blind in this world rather they walked the straight path of guidance, in the full light of knowledge, with open eyes.

translation.text: Verily We exalted them in consideration of a sterling quality: their remembrance of the Abode of the Hereafter.

commentary.text: Their success emanated from that fact that there was nothing of worldliness in their character. All their efforts, mental and physical, were directed towards the Hereafter. They remembered it themselves and urged others also to remember it. That is why Allah SWT exalted them to such high ranks as have never been attained by those who remained absorbed in earning worldly wealth and prosperity.

Allah SWT here has used the word ad-dar (that abode, or the real abode) for the Hereafter. This is meant to impress the truth that this world is no abode for man but only a passage and a rest house, which man has to leave. The real abode is the abode of the Hereafter.

translation.text: And remember Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhu al-Kifl. All were of the best.

sections.title: 49-64 AL-QURAN IS BUT A REMINDER ABOUT THE REWARD OF PARADISE AND PUNISHMENT OF THE HELLFIRE

translation.text: This was a remembrance. An excellent retreat awaits the God-fearing
everlasting Gardens with gates wide open for them

commentary.text: Allah tells us that His blessed, believing servants will have a good final return

The angels appointed for keeping Paradise will open the gates for them as soon as they see them. When they arrive and its gates shall already have been opened, its keepers will say: Peace be upon you, you have fared well, enter here to dwell forever. (Surah Az-Zumar, Ayat 73).
Al-Rayyan is the door in paradise for those who fast in abundance.

translation.text: wherein they shall recline, wherein they shall ask for abundant fruit and drinks,

commentary.text: Whatever they ask for, they will find it, and it will be prepared just as they wanted it and served to the residents of Heaven.

translation.text: and wherein there shall be with them well-matched, bashful mates.

commentary.text: "Of equal age” may mean that they will be of equal age/beauty among themselves, and also that they will be of the same age as their spouses. No disputes or animosity between them.

translation.text: All this is what you are promised for the Day of Judgement.
This is Our provision for you, never to end.

commentary.text: This is the reward/promise for those who have taqwa (Allah consciousness). Allah SWT's promises always come true. Then Allah SWT tells us that Paradise will never come to an end or disappear or cease to be.

translation.text: All this (is for the God-fearing). But for the transgressors, an evil resort awaits them

commentary.text: The Final Return of the Doomed

Having mentioned the final return for the blessed now Allah SWT mentions the final return of the doomed when they are resurrected and brought to account. Those who disobeyed will meet the worst final return -- Hell

translation.text: Hell, where they will be roasted. An evil place to dwell!

commentary.text: They will enter it and it will overwhelm them on all sides. Meaning it will be tight and constricting.

translation.text: All this (is for them); so let them taste boiling water and pus,

commentary.text: Let them taste boiling hot water. The word ghassaq (pus), have been given by lexicographers: (1) Any moisture that is discharged by the body in the form of pus, blood, or mixture of pus and blood, etc. and this includes tears as well. (2) Something extremely cold. (3) Something stinking and giving out offensive smell. However, the word is generally used in the first meaning only, though the other two meanings also are correct lexically.

translation.text: and other sufferings of the kind.

commentary.text: Suffering, such as intense cold and intense heat, and drinking Hamim (boiling hot water), eating the bitter tree of Az-Zaqqum and being lifted up and thrown down, and various other punishments.

translation.text: (Observing their followers advancing to Hell they will say, among themselves: “This is a troop rushing in to you. There is no welcome for them. They are destined to roast in the Fire.”

commentary.text: The Disputes of the People of Hell

Here Allah SWT tells us what the people of Hell (the leaders who lead others to falsehood) will say to one another. When a new tribe of disbelievers arrives in Hell they will not be greeted with a welcome instead with aversion and disgust. This is because Hell will already be so constricted and tight for space and air that when more people enter it will make it much worse.

translation.text: They will reply: “Rather, no welcome to you. (You will roast in Hell.) It is you who led us to this end. What an evil resort!”

commentary.text: Their followers will say: `you called us to that which led us to this fate.'  Evil is this abode and this destination. Blame game begins.

translation.text: They will say: “Our Lord, give twofold punishment in the Fire to him who has led us to this.”

commentary.text: They will ask Allah to give the people who mislead them twice the punishment.

translation.text: They will say to one another: “But why do we not see those whom we considered him among the wicked?

commentary.text: They will look around bewildered and will find only themselves and their guides/leaders in Hell but will find no trace of those people of whom they used to talk disparagingly in the world, and whom they used to mock for believing in God, the Messenger and the Hereafter.

translation.text: Is it that we mistakenly made fun of them; or have they disappeared from our sight?”

commentary.text: Lesson: Sometimes people are perceived falsely so investigate/ understand for yourself what the truth is.

translation.text: Verily all this is true. This is how the inmates of the Fire will dispute among themselves.

commentary.text: In hell love and friendship will turn to hate.  Allah SWT says: This is the truth (Haq) – This will happen!
LESSON: ANYONE ENCOURAGING YOU MOVE AWAY FROM ALLAH SWT IS INDEED YOUR GREATEST ENEMY!!

sections.title: 65-70 THE MISSION OF THE RASOOLS' IS TO WARN PEOPLE AND DECLARE THAT THERE IS NO DIVINITY EXCEPT ALLAH

translation.text: Tell them, (O Prophet): “I am nothing but a warner. There is no deity but Allah, the One, the Supreme,

commentary.text: The Message of the Messenger is a Great News

Now the discourse turns to the same theme with which it began. One should read it keeping Ayat 1-4 in mind in order to fully understand the meaning. In Ayat 4 it was said: The people wonder why a warner from among themselves has come to them.

Here it is being said: Tell them: I (Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) am only a warner. If you do not listen to me and do not accept my message, you will only be causing a loss to yourselves. If you continue to remain in ignorance and heedlessness soon you will see your end yourselves.

translation.text: the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is in between them, the Most Mighty, the Most Forgiving.”

commentary.text: This is the answer to what the disbelievers said in Ayat 5: Has he made just One God in place of all the gods? This is indeed a strange thing. The mushriks said: Deities are many of whom one is Allah also. How is it that you have done away with all other deities and kept only One Allah?

In answer it was said: The real Deity is One Allah alone, for He is dominant over everything: He is the Owner of the earth and the heavens, and everything in the Universe belongs to Him. Every being other than Him, whom you have set up as other gods in the Universe, is dominated, subservient and subdued before Him. Therefore, there is no ground for which they may be regarded as deities.
So give up your false pride and repent!

translation.text: Say, “This ˹Quran˺ is momentous news,
from which you are turning away.”

commentary.text: The Quran brings us admonition, advice and guidance. There is no greater or more urgent news than the Day of Judgment.

sections.title: 71-88 STORY OF THE CREATION OF ADAM AND DISOBEDIENCE OF IBLEES (SHAITAN)

translation.text: When your Lord said to the angels: “Verily I am creating a human being from clay.

commentary.text: The Story of Adam and Iblis/satan
This is the seventh and last time the story of Iblis/satan is mentioned in the Quran.

Before creating Adam, peace be upon him, Allah SWT told the angels that He was going to create a human being from sounding clay of altered smooth black mud. He told them that when He finished creating and forming him, they were to prostrate to him as a sign of honor and respect, and out of obedience to the command of Allah SWT, may He be exalted.

All of the angels obeyed this command except for Iblis/satan, who was not one of them. He was one of the Jinn, and his nature betrayed him at his time of greatest need. He refused to prostrate to Adam, and he disputed with his Lord about him, claiming that he was better than Adam, because he was created from fire while Adam was created from clay, and fire was better than clay, or so he said.

He made a mistake by doing this, and he went against the command of Allah SWT, thus committing the sin of disbelief. So, Allah SWT exiled him, humiliated him, and cast him out of His mercy and His sacred Presence, and called him "Iblis/satan'' symbolizing that he had Ablasa min Ar-Rahmah (despaired of mercy) -- that there was no hope for him of mercy. He cast him down from the heavens, disgraced and rejected, to the earth.

Iblis/satan asked Allah SWT to give him a reprieve until the Day of Resurrection, and so Allah SWT gave him a reprieve. When he knew that he was safe from destruction until the Day of Resurrection, he rebelled and transgressed.

This story has already been narrated at the following places: (Surah Al- Baqarah, Ayats 30-39); (Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayats 11-25); (Surah Al-Hijr, Ayats 26-44); (Surah Bani Israil, Ayats 61-65); (Surah Al-Kahf, Ayat 50); (Surah TaHa, Ayats 116-126).

translation.text: After I have created him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall you down, prostrating yourselves to him.”

commentary.text: For explanation, see (Surah Al-Hijr, Ayats 29-30), and (E.N. 16 of Surah As-Sajdah).
For explanation, see (Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayats 34); (Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayat 11)

translation.text: Then the angels, all of them, prostrated themselves before Adam
except Iblis/satan. He waxed proud and became one of the unbelievers.

commentary.text: For explanation, see (Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayat 34); (Surah Al-Kahf, Ayat 50)

arabic_lines: قَالَ يٰۤـاِبۡلِيۡسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ اَنۡ تَسۡجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقۡتُ بِيَدَىَّ ؕ اَسۡتَكۡبَرۡتَ اَمۡ كُنۡتَ مِنَ الۡعَالِيۡ

translation.text: Allah asked, “O Iblîs! What prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My Own Hands? Did you ˹just˺ become proud? Or have you always been arrogant?”

commentary.text: These words have been used to point out the honor, rank and glory bestowed on man by his Creator. In other words, Allah SWT did not get man created through his angels but created man Himself because man’s creation was a highly noble task. Therefore, what is meant to be said is: ‘What has prevented you from prostrating yourself before him whom I have made directly Myself

The words 'be-yadaiia,' (both hands) probably are meant to refer to the fact that this new creation combines in itself two important aspects of Allah SWT’s power of creation: (1) That man has been given an animal body on account of which he belongs to the animal kingdom. (2) That on account of the Spirit/Ruh breathed into him, he has been characterized with qualities that place him in honor and merit above all earthly creations and creatures.

translation.text: He replied: “I am nobler than he. You created me from fire and created him from clay.”
He said: “Get out of here; surely you are accursed,

commentary.text: Lexically, the word rajim, as used in the original, means “cast off” and in common usage it is used for the person, who has been thrown down from a place of honor and humiliated.
ALLAH SWT'S CURSE IS WITH IBLIS/SATAN.

translation.text: and My curse shall remain upon you till the Day of Resurrection.

commentary.text: Iblis/satan will remain accursed till the Day of Judgment because of his disobedience, and after the Day of Judgment he will be punished for the sins that he will have committed from the creation of Adam until Resurrection.

translation.text: Satan said: “My Lord, then grant me respite till the Day that they are raised up.”
He said: “You are of those who have been granted respite
till the Day whose Hour I know.”
(Iblis/satan) said: “By Your glory, I shall mislead them all
except those of Your servants, the chosen ones from amongst them.”

commentary.text: This does not mean: I will not lead Your chosen servants astray, but it means: I shall have no power over Your chosen servants because their focus and aim in life is different i.e the end game for them is the Hereafter.

translation.text: He (i.e. Allah) said: “This is the Truth and I only speak the Truth
I will certainly fill the Gehenna (Hell) with you and with all those among them who follow you.”

commentary.text: Iblis/satan and his whole army of the satans who will be joining him in misleading mankind till Resurrection.
This entire story has been related in answer to this saying of the chiefs of the Quraysh: Was he the only (fit) person among us to whom Allah SWT’s admonition should have been sent down?

Its first answer was the one given in Ayat 9-10, saying: Are you the owners of the treasures of the mercy of your Mighty and Bounteous Lord? And does the kingdom of the heavens and the earth belong to you, and is it for you to decide as to who should be appointed God’s Prophet and who should not be appointed?

In the second answer the chiefs of the Quraysh have been told: Your jealousy, your pride and arrogance against Muhammad (peace be upon him) are similar to the jealousy and arrogance of Iblis/satan against Adam (peace be upon him). Iblis/satan had also refused to acknowledge the right of Allah SWT to appoint anyone He pleased as His vicegerent, and you are also refusing to acknowledge His right to appoint anyone He pleases as His Messenger.

Iblis/satan disobeyed the command to bow down before Adam, and you are disobeying the command to follow Muhammad (PBUH). Your resemblance with him does not end here, but your fate also will be the same as has been pre-ordained for him, i.e. the curse of God in the world and the fire of Hell in the Hereafter.

Besides the above two other things also have been stressed: (1) Whoever is disobeying Allah SWT in this world, is in fact, falling a prey to Iblis/satan, his eternal enemy, who has resolved to mislead and misguide mankind since the beginning of creation. (2) The one who disobeys Allah SWT on account of arrogance and persists in His disobedience is under His wrath: such a one has no forgiveness from Him.

translation.text: This is nothing but an Admonition for all people the world over.
You will know the truth of the matter after a while.”

commentary.text: The Quran is an admonition and a reminder of ALL (Ayat 1). Very soon (after death) the special news or the truth will become apparent to ALL.

Lastly the same theme of Tawhid and Prophet hood is once again reiterated.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makki Surah.  It was revealed most probably sometime before the Hijrah of Abyssinia.  It has 75 Ayats in 8 Rukus.

front_matter.label: Subject and Topics
front_matter.text:
The entire Surah is a most eloquent and effective address that was given some time before the emigration to Habash, in an environment filled with tyranny, persecution, ill-will and antagonism. It is a sermon whose addressees mainly are the unbelieving Quraysh, although here and there the believers also have been addressed.

This Surah deals almost exclusively with the issue of God’s oneness or Tawhid (both in word and in action). Its aim is to convey that man should adopt Allah's servitude sincerely and not pollute his God worship with the servitude to any other (shirk). This cardinal principle has been presented in different ways over and over again.

In this regard, believers have been instructed that: 'If a place has become too constricted for the worship and service of Allah SWT, His earth is vast: you may emigrate to some other place in order to save your faith. Allah SWT will reward you for your patience.

The Holy Prophet has been encouraged to: 'Tell the disbelievers plainly that they may do whatever they like but their persecutions and tyrannies should never deter you from the way of Islam; that they may go on doing their worst to obstruct your way but you will continue to perform your mission in spite of the adverse conditions and circumstances.'

sections.title: 1-9 MUSHRIKIN TRY TO JUSTIFY THEIR WORSHIP TO SAINTS SAYING THAT IT MAY BRING US CLOSER TO ALLAH AND ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT NO BEARER OF BURDEN SHALL BEAR THE BURDEN OF ANOTHER

arabic_lines: تَنۡزِيۡلُ الۡكِتٰبِ مِنَ اللّٰهِ الۡعَزِيۡزِ الۡحَكِيۡمِ

translation.text: The revelation of this Book is from Allah, the Most Mighty, the Most Wise.

commentary.text: The Order for Tawhid and the Refutation of Shirk

Allah SWT tells us that the revelation of this Book, which is the magnificent Quran, is from Him, and is the truth in which there is no doubt whatsoever. The Quran is not Muhammad’s (PBUH) word, as the disbelievers assert, but it is Allah SWT’s Word, which He Himself has sent down.
SO DO NOT TREAT THIS AS ANY OTHER BOOK.

Two of Allah SWT's attributes have been mentioned to warn the listeners of two realities so that they do not underestimate this Word but understand its full importance: (1) Allah SWT is All-Mighty; الۡعَزِيۡزِ that is, He is so powerful that no power can prevent His will and decisions from being enforced and none can dare resist Him in any way. (2) He is All-wise الۡحَكِيۡمِ; that is, the guidance He is giving in this Book, is wholly based on wisdom and only an ignorant and foolish person will turn away from it.
(For further explanation, see (E.N. 1 of Surah As-Sajdah).

arabic_lines: اِنَّاۤ اَنۡزَلۡنَاۤ اِلَيۡكَ الۡكِتٰبَ بِالۡحَقِّ فَاعۡبُدِ اللّٰهَ مُخۡلِصًا لَّهُ الدِّيۡنَ

translation.text: (O Prophet), it is We Who have revealed this Book to you with Truth. So serve only Allah, consecrating (purifying/dedicating) your devotion to Him.

commentary.text: This is a very important Ayat that states the real objective of the message of Islam. Therefore, one should not pass over it superficially, but should try to understand its meaning and intention.

The status of the Quran is being established here. Approach the Quran with the full faith that it contains nothing but the truth and there is no element of falsehood in it. Worship Allah SWT Alone with no partner or associate and call mankind to that.
Ibadat is derived from abd عْبُدِ, and this word is used for a freeman i.e. not a slave or bonded servant.

Thus, the demand is to worship Allah SWT in a holistic manner, that is, not only worship Allah SWT EXCLUSIVELY via words but also via deeds. Merely uttering the kalam shahadah is not enough we must also worship Allah SWT exclusively via our actions -- obeying His commands and laws in totality with sincerity and love.
Hence, man cannot say he worships Allah SWT if he makes his desires his god and lives on sheer human/animalistic instincts alone, i.e., eat, sleep, go to work, raise children, etc.

translation.text: Indeed, sincere devotion is due only to Allah. As for those who take other lords besides Him, saying, “We worship them only so they may bring us closer to Allah,” surely Allah will judge between all regarding what they differed about. Allah certainly does not guide whoever persists in lying and disbelief.

commentary.text: (Also see Ayat 2)

The best commentary of this Ayat is the Hadith: A person asked the Prophet (PBUH): We give away our wealth so that we become well-known. Shall we get a reward for this? The Prophet (PBUH) replied: No. He asked: What, if one has the intention both of Allah SWT's reward and of reputation in this world? The Holy Prophet replied: Allah SWT does not accept any deed unless it is performed EXCLUSIVELY for His sake. Then he recited this same verse.
“We worship them only so they may bring us closer to Allah….(39:3)

The disbelievers of Makkah and even today some say the same: ‘The Creator is only Allah, and He alone is the real Deity; but He is too high for us to have access to Him. Therefore, we make these saintly beings or Pirs or idols just a means to convey our prayers and our petitions to Allah SWT. This is a doctrine that has spread among the people on account of superstitions, whims and blind imitation of their elders.
Allah certainly does not guide whoever persists in lying and disbelief….(39:3)
Allah SWT does not guide those who are kazib (liars) and kafir (denier/disbeliever/ungrateful).
They have been called kazib (liar) because they have falsely invented this doctrine and then spread falsehood among others.

As for kafir it has two meanings: (1) A stubborn disbeliever (2) someone who is ungrateful for blessings, i.e. they are receiving all kinds of blessings from Allah SWT, but are thanking other beings assuming that these blessings are reaching them through their influence.
It is Allah SWT’s EXCLUSIVE right that He should be obeyed and worshiped sincerely. Do not be halfhearted in worship.
Allah SWT says enter Islam fully.
(2:208) O Believers, enter completely into Islam and do not follow in" the footsteps of Satan, for he is your avowed enemy
Lesson: Do not rely on others to inform you about religion. Educate yourself re: what constitutes ‘shirk/falsehood,’ both generally and specific to your biggest weakness re: ‘shirk.’

translation.text: If Allah had wanted to take to Himself a son, He could have chosen anyone He wanted out of those whom He creates.8 Glory be to Him (that He should have a son). He is Allah: the One, the Overpowering.

commentary.text: One creator (Allah SWT) the rest are His creation!

translation.text: If you disbelieve, know well that Allah has no need of you. Yet He does not like unbelief in His servants. But if you are thankful, your thankfulness will please Him. No one shall bear another's burden. You are destined to return to your Lord and He will tell you what you used to do. He is well aware even of what lies hidden in your breasts.

commentary.text: Allah hates Disbelief and is pleased with Gratitude
If you disbelieve, know well that Allah has no need of you….(39:7)

Your disbelief cannot cause any decrease or deficiency in His Kingdom. He will be God if you believe in Him, and He will still be God if you deny Him. According to Hadith (Muslim), Allah SWT says: O My servants, if all of you, the former and the latter, the men and the jinns, become like the heart of a most sinful person among you, it will cause no deficiency whatever in My Kingdom.

Here, one should bear in mind the fact that Allah SWT’s will is one thing and His approval and pleasure another. Nothing in the world can happen against Allah SWT’s will, but many things can happen against His approval, For example, wickedness/mischief in the world, the existence of thieves and robbers, the presence of murderers and adulterers, are possible only because Allah SWT has made room for the occurrence of these evils and the existence of these criminals in the scheme of things ordained by Him.
….Yet He does not like unbelief in His servants…..(39:7)

Allah says: If you want to disbelieve (kufur), you may do so. We will not stop you from this nor make you believe forcibly. But We do not approve that you should deny your Creator and Provider, being His servants, for it is harmful for yourselves -- disbelief is harmful to yourself.
…..But if you are thankful, your thankfulness will please Him…(39:7)

The word shukr (gratitude) has been used here against kufur (disbelief). This by itself shows that kufur (disbelief) is, in fact, ingratitude and disloyalty. The person who has any feeling of the favors of Allah Almighty, cannot adopt any other way than that of belief and faith. Therefore, gratitude and faith are correlatives. Wherever there is gratitude there will be faith also. On the contrary, wherever there is disbelief, there will be no question of gratitude at all, for gratitude along with disbelief is meaningless.
…..No one shall bear another's burden…..(39:7)

It means: If a person adopts disbelief in order to please others or to avoid their displeasure, then do not expect that they will never bear the burden of our disbelief. Each one of us is responsible for our deeds.

translation.text: When any affliction befalls man, he cries out to his Lord, penitently turning to Him. But when his Lord bestows His favour upon him, he forgets the affliction regarding which he had cried out and sets up compeers to Allah that they may lead others astray from His Path. Say, (O Prophet): “Enjoy your unbelief for a while. Surely you will be among the inmates of the Fire.”

commentary.text: Also see (39:49)
It is an aspect of Man's Disbelief that He remembers Allah at times of difficulty then associates others with Him after He has been relieved of His Distress

At the time of a calamity/difficulty or distress man turns only to Allah, Lord of the worlds. This is a clear proof of the fact that in the depths of his heart he understands that all other deities are helpless and has the realization that Allah SWT alone is the possessor of all powers and authority -- even if this lies buried and hidden deep in his mind. Yet, after the affliction that had befallen him has been averted, he asserts that this has been averted via the help of such and such a pious man or saint, or god/goddess. Thus, many others then also put their faith in these deities besides Allah SWT and are further misled.

sections.title: 10-18 BELIEVERS WHO CANNOT PRACTICE THEIR FAITH (ISLAM) SHOULD MIGRATE TO OTHER PLACES WHERE THEY CAN AND THE REAL LOSERS ARE THOSE WHO SHALL LOSE THEIR SOULS AND THEIR FAMILIES ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT

translation.text: Tell them (O Prophet): “O you servants of Mine who believe, have fear of your Lord. A good end awaits those who did good in this world.  Allah's earth is spacious. Verily those who persevere shall be granted their reward beyond all reckoning.”

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Iman + good deeds = success
The Command for Taqwa, Emigration and to worship Him alone with all Sincerity
Act according to what Allah SWT has enjoined and avoid what He has forbidden and live in the world fearing His accountability. This will lead to success in this life as well as the next in sha Allah.

If one city, territory or land has become difficult for the worshipers of Allah SWT, then emigrate to another place where you do not have to face such hardships. Allah SWT's earth is vast and plentiful.

arabic_lines: قُلۡ اِنِّىۡۤ اُمِرۡتُ اَنۡ اَعۡبُدَ اللّٰهَ مُخۡلِصًا لَّهُ الدِّيۡنَۙ

translation.text: Tell them, (O Prophet): “I am bidden to serve Allah, consecrating my devotion to Him,

commentary.text: Also see (Ayat 2, 3)

Exclusive worship of Allah SWT: Meaning 100 per cent not 10 per cent nor 20 per cent but 100 per cent Exclusive worship of Allah SWT is acceptable. And nothing less. EXCLUSIVE AND COMPLETE SUBMISSION and obedience to Allah SWT.

Ibbadat or worship has two aspects to it: (i) complete submission and obedience to Allah SWT coupled with (ii) the sincere love and devotion for Allah SWT. These two aspects coupled with the rituals of deen i.e. salah, zikr etc. = worship.
The curx of this Surah is the man’s ibbadat of Allah SWT should not become polluted in the first two aspects mentioned above. Do not join anyone else in the COMPLETE SUBMISSION and LOVE of Allah SWT.

translation.text: Say: “Allah alone shall I serve, consecrating my devotion to Him.

commentary.text: Also see (Ayat 2, 3 and 11)
Again, we find an emphasis on Tawhid. No other religion takes monotheism as seriously as Islam.

translation.text: So serve, apart from Him, whomsoever you please.” Say: “Behold, the real losers shall be those who will have lost their own selves and their kith and kin on the Day of Resurrection. Behold, that is the obvious loss.

commentary.text: DEFINATION OF LOSS = Shirk (worship of false gods i.e. money, job, desires etc.)

Not only has man-incurred loss for himself by committing shirk but has caused the same loss for his children, near and dear ones, friends and fellow countrymen by his wrong education, training and example, which is why Allah SWT has called this khusran-i-mubin (most obvious loss).
Not only are you going straight to Hell but also taking (others) your family and friends with you.

arabic_lines: الَّذِيۡنَ يَسۡتَمِعُوۡنَ الۡقَوۡلَ فَيَتَّبِعُوۡنَ اَحۡسَنَهٗ ؕ اُولٰٓـئِكَ الَّذِيۡنَ هَدٰٮهُمُ اللّٰهُ وَاُولٰٓـئِكَ هُمۡ اُولُوا الۡاَلۡبَابِ

translation.text: to those who pay heed to what is said and follow the best of it (Ahsaan). They are the ones whom Allah has guided to the Right Way; they are the ones endowed with understanding.

commentary.text: (Also see 39:55)

There are varying grades/levels in religion (deen): (i) Islam, (ii) Iman and then (iii) Ahsaan. Those who strive for Ahsaan or the best in religion are being mentioned here. Those who aim high. When they hear something/anything they interpret the best meaning from it and then they follow the best. They listen attentively and reflect. They possess sound reasoning and an upright nature. They are the ones whom Allah SWT guides in this world and the Hereafter.

True knowledge and intelligence that the Quran imparts is to ability to recognize who our creator is and what our purpose in life is i.e. the worship of Allah SWT. So do not be deluded by those who have PHD's in physics etc. Although that too is good but true intelligence/wisdom is mentioned here.

Lesson: Most of us strive our utmost for this world however in religion we are willing to comprise and do the very least possible so as to just to scarp by. Reflect upon yourself -- What are my priorities and what am I striving towards?

sections.title: 19-21 NO ONE CAN RESCUE THE ONE AGAINST WHOM THE SENTENCE OF PUNISHMENT HAS BEEN DECREED

translation.text: (O Prophet), can you save him (from chastisement) against whom the sentence of chastisement has become due; him who has, (as it were), already fallen into the Fire?”

commentary.text: Can you rescue someone who is already in the fire? Prophet (PBUH) being comforted – it's as if these disbelievers (of Makkah) are already in the fire so don’t worry about them. Instead focus on those people who want to be guided.

translation.text: But those who fear their Lord shall have lofty mansions built over one another beneath which rivers flow. This is Allah's promise and never does Allah fail to fulfil His promise.

commentary.text: Conversely, those who have Taqwa or Allah consciousness, for them are multiple skyscrapers/palaces and mansions as homes in Paradise. And Allah SWT's promise always comes true.

sections.title: 22-31 AL-QURAN IS CONSISTENT IN ITS VERSES YET REPEATS ITS TEACHINGS IN DIFFERENT WAYS AND ALLAH HAS CITED EVERY KIND OF PARABLE IN AL-QURAN SO THAT PEOPLE MAY LEARN A LESSON

translation.text: Can he whose breast Allah has opened up for Islam and who is thus (moving along a Path) illumined by a light from Allah (be likened to him who derives no lesson from what he observes)? Woe, then, to those whose hearts were further hardened after Allah's admonition. Such are indeed in obvious error.

commentary.text: A person whose chest has been opened up for Islam is someone who accepts and lives by Islam. Now he/she is upon guidance (Nur) and thus life is much easier as there is no anxiety or ambiguity/doubt in his/her mind.  Nor is there a feeling of any danger and loss in accepting and adopting the deen, rather full satisfaction of the heart.
….(moving along a Path) illumined by a light from Allah…(39:22)

The light is the Nur of guidance i.e Quran and Sunnah via which he/she clearly sees every step towards the straight path of the truth among the countless by-paths of life. With guidance, knowledge and clarity he/she is not deceived by what is in this world.
Conversely, destruction is for those whose hearts are hard for the zikr of Allah SWT. Firstly, they refuse to read the Quran and when they do they are unaffected by it.
One is a person whose heart expands with the Quran.
The other is whose heart feels distressed or is constricted by the Quran.

Allah SWT says that the person who reaches the second state/stage is totally ruined. Here also was a warning for those who were bent upon stubbornness in their antagonism towards the Prophet (PBUH) and had made up their mind not to listen to him at all. For this they have been warned, as if to say: You take pride in this stubbornness of yours, but, as a matter of fact, there cannot be a greater misfortune and unworthiness of man than that his heart should become even more hardened, instead of becoming soft, when he hears Allah being mentioned and the admonition sent by Him.
Three motifs mentioned in one Ayat that are mentioned in the Quran over and over again:
Nur = Guidance and Darkness = Ignorance (disbelief)
Soft Heart = Pure, humble, gentle Heart.  Hard Heart = Heart full of pride, self-centered, cruel
Opening of the Heart = Islam and Constriction of Heart = Disbelief

translation.text: Allah has revealed the best teaching, a self-consistent Book which repeats its contents in manifold forms whereat shiver the skins of those that hold their Lord in awe, and then their skins and their hearts soften for Allah's remembrance. That is Allah's Guidance wherewith He guides whosoever He pleases. And he whom Allah does not guide to the Right Path has none to guide him.

commentary.text: The Description of the Quran
Allah SWT has sent down the best clear speech (ahassan hadith) اَللّٰهُ نَزَّلَ اَحۡسَنَ الۡحَدِيۡثِ

as there is no contradiction in it. The whole Book, from the beginning to the end, projects one and the same aim, one and the same belief, and one and the same system of thought and action. Each of its parts confirms, supports and explains the other themes; and there is perfect consistency in it both in meaning and in style. Concepts are mentioned in pairs i.e. Heaven and Hell, good and evil, reward and punishment, fear and hope, commands and prohibitions etc. Seven times the story of Adam and Iblis is mentioned so as to drive home a point yet every time the story highlights a new aspect thus it is always interesting and engaging.
…..their skins and their hearts soften for Allah's remembrance….(39:23)
The physical manifestation the Quran has upon the believers is that their skin trembles with fear and then their hearts and skin soften with the remembrance of Allah SWT.

Those who have fear and hope – together -- are physically affected when reading the Quran. Allah SWT is most definitely the most merciful so there is hope but never forget that Allah SWT also punishes those who disobey so be fearful as well.

translation.text: We have indeed propounded (offered) for mankind all kinds of parables in this Qur'an that they may take heed.

commentary.text: Examples/parables are given in the Quran to make matters clear. So, take heed, reflect, understand and learn. Allah SWT has not deprived people of clear guidance – thus then punishment is earned.

translation.text: It is an Arabic Quran free of all crookedness that they may guard against their evil end.

commentary.text: The Quran has not been sent down in a foreign language so that the people of Makkah and Arabia need a translator or interpreter, but it is in their own language, which they can understand directly. Also, there is nothing duplicitous in it so that a common man should find it difficult to understand. Everything has been presented in a straightforward manner from which everyone can know what this Book states as wrong and why, what it states as right and on what grounds, what it wants the people to accept and what it wants them to reject and what it enjoins and what it forbids.
Everything in the Quran is full of Khair/blessing. It will save people not put them in danger.

translation.text: Allah propounds (sets forth) a parable: there is a man whose ownership is shared by several quarrelsome masters, each pulling him to himself; and there is another who is exclusively owned by one man. Can the two be alike? All praise and thanks be to Allah. But most of them are unaware.

commentary.text: The Parable of Shirk
Allah SWT in this parable has explained the difference between Shirk and Tawhid and the impact each has on human life -- in a clear and concise manner.

The example is of a man who has many masters and all have equal rights over him. Each master is pulling him in a different direction; thus no one is content. And each command contradicts the commands of the other masters. All the masters are ill-tempered and demanding so no one is satisfied or happy.

On the contrary, the person, who is the slave or servant of only one master, a master who is kind and good. With the absence of competing masters, the servant can concentrate on his duties thus, having a happy master and happy servant.

This is a straightforward example. In Islam we submit to One Master – Allah SWT. After this it remains no longer difficult for a person to understand that the peace of mind and satisfaction that accrue from the service of One God, can never accrue from the service of many gods/deities/idols or things like one’s own desires or the unrelenting pursual of fame/money/people etc. that keep man in a constant state of unease and contentedness.

Allah SWT asks are these two equals? Al-hamdulillah: Thank God that you too appreciate the difference between the two situations and none among you can dare say that slavery to many masters is better than slavery to one master, or that both are equal. But when you are made to understand the difference between God-worship and the worship of many gods, you show lack of understanding.
